**The explanation of the ta'wil (interpretation) of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah." Say, "Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?"﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate others with Allah: "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and their Manager?" They will say, "Allah." Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say, "Allah." So He said to him: Say, O Muhammad: "Its Lord, who created it and brought it into being, is the One for whom worship alone is fitting, and He is Allah." Then He said: If they answer you with that, then say to them: "Have you then taken, besides the Lord of the heavens and the earth, protectors that do not possess for themselves any benefit that they might bring to themselves, nor any harm that they might ward off from themselves? And since they do not possess that for themselves, then possessing it for others is even further away. Yet you worship them, and you have abandoned the worship of the One in whose hand are benefit and harm, life and death, and the management of all things." Then, may His praise be exalted, He set forth for them an example, saying: ﴿Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal?"﴾

* *

**The explanation of the ta'wil of His saying: ﴿Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darknesses and the light equal? Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed alike to them?" Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer."﴾ (16)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worship, besides Allah, the One in whose hand is their benefit and harm, that which neither benefits nor harms: ﴿Are the blind equal?﴾ — the one who sees nothing and is not guided to a road to travel except when he is led — ﴿and the seeing?﴾ — the one who guides the blind to the road, the one who sees nothing? Surely they are not equal, without doubt. He means: likewise, the believer who sees the truth and follows it, and recognizes guidance and takes its path, is not equal to you, O polytheists, who do not recognize truth and do not perceive right direction.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or are the darknesses and the light equal?﴾ — His, the Exalted's, saying means: Are the darknesses, in which the path is not seen and the way is not perceived so as to be traveled, equal to the light, by which things are seen and whose brightness dispels the darkness? He means: These two are surely not equal, without doubt. Likewise, disbelief in Allah: its possessor is in bewilderment, forever wandering in confusion, never returning to any reality. And faith in Allah: its possessor is in illumination, acting with knowledge of his Lord, and with awareness that there is one who will reward him for his good deeds, one who will punish him for his evil deeds, one who will provide for him, and one who will benefit him.

Or are the darknesses and the light equal?"﴾ As for ﴿the blind and the seeing﴾, it is the disbeliever and the believer; and as for ﴿the darknesses and the light﴾, it is guidance and misguidance.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed alike to them?﴾ — His, the Exalted's, saying means: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: Did your idols, which you have taken as protectors besides Allah, create a creation like the creation of Allah, so that their affair became confused to you regarding what they created and what Allah created, and therefore you made them partners to Him? Or is it rather that ignorance and straying from what is right have overtaken you? For it is not unclear to anyone of sound intellect that worshipping what neither harms nor benefits is ignorance, and that worship is fitting only for the One whose benefit is hoped for and whose harm is feared. Just as the error of that and the ignorance of its doer are not unclear, so too the ignorance of one who associates in worship with the One who provides for him, sustains him, and supports him, is not unclear, when the one he associates with has no power over harm or benefit.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:** ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is foam like it. Thus does God strike the parable of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits people remains on the earth. Thus does God strike the parables﴾ (13:17).

Abu Ja'far said: This is a parable that God struck for truth and falsehood, and for belief and disbelief.

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: The likeness of truth in its stability, and of falsehood in its vanishing, is the likeness of water that God sent down from the sky to the earth. ﴿So the valleys flowed according to their measure﴾, meaning: the valleys carried it according to their capacity, the large according to its size and the small according to its size. ﴿So the torrent carried a swelling foam﴾, meaning: the torrent that arose from that water which God sent down from the sky carried foam rising high above the flood.

This is one of the two parables of truth and falsehood. Truth is the lasting water that God sent down from the sky, and the foam that brings no benefit is falsehood.

The second parable is: ﴿And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, says: This is another parable of truth and falsehood. It is like silver or gold that people heat in the fire, seeking an ornament they make or goods, and that (metal) is of copper, lead, and iron, which is heated so that goods may be made from it that are beneficial. ﴿There is foam like it﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says: From these things that they heat there is foam like it, meaning: like the foam of the torrent, which brings no benefit and goes away as vanity, just as the foam of the torrent brings no benefit and goes away as vanity.

* *

The word "foam" (zabad) is in the nominative case by virtue of His words ﴿from that which they heat in the fire﴾.

* *

The meaning of the statement is: From what they heat in the fire there is foam, like the foam of the torrent in its quick passing away, while the pure gold and silver remain.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Thus does God strike the parable of truth and falsehood﴾, meaning: just as God struck the parable of belief and disbelief [[In the printed edition: "as God struck the parable of belief..", the passage omitted here is restored from the manuscript]] concerning the swift passing away of disbelief and the ruin of its holder when God requites him, with the lasting beneficial water of the torrent and the pure gold and silver, so God likewise strikes the parable of truth and falsehood. ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾, meaning: as for the foam that rises over the torrent and over the gold, silver, copper, and lead when they are heated, it passes away by the thrust of the winds and by the water casting it off, and by its clinging to the trees and the sides of the valley. ﴿But what benefits people﴾, of the water, gold, silver, lead, and copper: as for the water, it remains in the earth so that it is drunk, and as for the gold and silver, they remain for people. ﴿Thus does God strike the parables﴾, meaning: just as He struck this parable for belief and disbelief, so He strikes the parables.

Thus does God strike the parable of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾, and "al-judha'" (scum) is what clings to the trees. ﴿But what benefits people remains on the earth﴾. These are three parables that God struck in one likeness. He says: Just as this foam vanishes and becomes scum that brings no benefit and whose blessing is not hoped for, so falsehood vanishes from its people just as this foam vanished, and just as this water remained on the earth, so that land became green and brought forth its plants, so truth remains for its people just as this water remained in the earth, and by it God brought forth what it brought forth of plants. His words: ﴿And from that which you heat in the fire﴾, the verse: just as the pure gold and silver remain when they are put into the fire and their dross goes away, so truth remains for its people. His words: ﴿or goods, there is foam like it﴾: He says: This iron and brass, from which benefits are derived. He says: Just as the pure part of this iron and this brass remains when they are put into the fire and their dross goes away, so truth remains for its people just as their pure part remained.

2031 [20320]- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿the valleys flowed according to their measure﴾, the large according to its measure and the small according to its measure= ﴿a swelling foam﴾, he said: It rose above the water, the foam. "And from that which you heat in the fire," he said: It is gold; when it is put in the fire, its purity remains and its impurity is removed. This is a parable God struck for truth and falsehood. ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾, it clings to the trees, so it becomes nothing. This is a parable of falsehood. ﴿But what benefits people remains on the earth﴾, and this brings forth plants. It is a parable of truth. ﴿Or goods, there is foam like it﴾, he said: "The goods" are brass and iron.

2031 [20321]- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, he said: Hawdhah ibn Khalifah told us, he said: Awf told us, he said: It reached me concerning His words: ﴿He sent down water from the sky, and the valleys flowed according to their measure﴾, he said: It is only a parable God struck for truth and falsehood. ﴿The valleys flowed according to their measure﴾: the small according to its measure, the large according to its measure, and what is between them according to its measure. ﴿So the torrent carried a swelling foam﴾, he says: great. Wherever the water settles, the foam goes away as scum, and the wind carries it off so that it becomes nothing, and the clear water that benefits people remains, from which they drink and grow plants and gain benefit. ﴿Or goods, there is foam like it﴾: and like the foam is everything that is heated in the fire: gold, silver, copper, and iron, whose dross goes away and what benefits remains in their hands. The dross and the scum are like falsehood, and what benefits people, of what is gathered in their hands, is the wealth that is in their hands.

2031 [20322]- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "And from that which you heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is foam like it": He said: This is a parable God struck for truth and falsehood. Then he recited: ﴿He sent down water from the sky, and the valleys flowed according to their measure, and the torrent carried a swelling foam﴾: this foam does not benefit. ﴿Or goods, there is foam like it﴾: this also does not benefit. He said: The water remained in the earth and benefited people, and the ornament that was made fit from this remained, and people benefited by it. ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits people remains on the earth. Thus does God strike the parables﴾. He said: This is a parable God struck for truth and falsehood.

2031 [20323]- Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, he said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿the valleys according to their measure﴾: the small according to its smallness and the large according to its largeness.

2031 [20324]- Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Talhah ibn Amr told us, from Ata': God struck a parable for truth and falsehood. He struck the parable of truth as the likeness of the torrent that remains in the earth, and He struck the parable of falsehood as the likeness of the foam that benefits no one.

* *

By His words ﴿rabiyan﴾, He means "high and swelling," from their saying: "rabā al-shay'" (the thing rose), "yarbū rubuwwan," so he is "rābin" (rising). From this the high ground like a hillock is called "rābiyah." From it is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿It stirs and swells﴾ [Surah al-Hajj 22:5 / Surah Fussilat 41:39]. [[See the explanation of "rabā" in earlier passages, 6:7.]]

* *

In this place, the brass, lead, and iron are called "al-matā'" (goods), because they are enjoyed, and everything from which people derive enjoyment is "matā'."

As the poet said: [[He is al-Mash'ath al-Amiri, and by this verse he was named "Mash'ath."]]

"Enjoy, O Mash'ath, for a thing
you have outrun by death is the goods"

[[Al-Asma'iyyat, no. 48; Mu'jam al-shu'ara', p. 475; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubaydah 1:328; Lisan (m-t-' root). These are excellent verses. After the verse he says: "By a burden the tribe leaves me one day, a pledge for their dwelling, and they are swift.

And there came a jay'al (a female hyena) and the father of her young, the one with the black eyelids of the eyes, with a limp and a hobble, so the two dug the dust over me, and what am I to do, woe to you, but the beasts of prey?"

He says: Let my death come, and my family leaves me buried in their dwelling, then they hasten away. Then the jay'al comes, which is the female of hyenas, and the male comes, black with eyelids and a limp, and the two dig up the dust over me, and I have no means of stopping what the two do.]]

* *

As for "al-judha'" (scum), I:

2031 [20325]- It was related to me from Abu Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: It is said: "The pot has overflowed (ajfa'at al-qidr)," and that is when it boils and its foam pours out, or when it calms and nothing remains of it. [[This is the exact text of Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:329.]]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra claimed that the meaning of His words ﴿it passes away as scum﴾ is that the earth absorbs it. He said: It is said: "The valley dried up (jafa al-wadi) and "ajfa," in the sense of drying out, and "the valley became dry (infajā al-wadi)" [[This is a text without parallel in the lexicons under the root (j-f-a), nor under (j-f-'), and it shows that he meant "jafa and ajfa," the weak final-radical verb, not the hamzated form. I do not know who said it.]], when the scum comes with that froth, and "the valley froths (ghathā al-wadi), it froths, a frothing and a foaming" [[I also do not know who said this before the time of Abu Ja'far, except that the author of Lisan mentioned something similar from Ibn Jinni, but what is known among the lexicographers is: "ghathā al-wadi yaghthū."]]. He mentioned that the Arabs say: "I skimmed the pot (jafa'tu al-qidr) and skim it (ajfa'uha)," when you take out its scum, which is the foam that rises on it. And "ajfa'tuha ijfa'an" is a dialect form. He said: They also say: "I threw the man down (jafa'tu al-rajul) with a throw (ja'fan)," meaning: I knocked him down.

It has been said that His words ﴿it passes away as scum﴾ mean "jafa'," because it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "The valley swept away its froth (jafa'a al-wadi ghuthā'ahu)," and it came out in the form of a noun, though it is a verbal noun. The Arabs do this with the verbal noun of anything in which some parts gather together upon others, like "qumāsh," "duqāq," "huttām," and "ghuthā'," which they bring out in the manner of a noun, as they did in their saying: "I gave him 'atā'" (a gift), meaning the giving. Had the verbal noun of "qumāsh" been intended in its proper form, it would be said: "He has gathered it, qamshan."

**The commentary on His words, the Exalted: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]; and those who did not respond to Him, [even] if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it. Those will have the worst accounting, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [13:18]**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention. He says: As for those who responded to God, by believing in Him when He called them to faith in Him, obeying Him, following His Messenger, and confirming what he brought them from God, ﴿for them is the best [reward]﴾, which is Paradise. [[See the explanation of "al-istijabah" (response) above, 13:465, note 4, and the references there.]] [[See the explanation of "al-husna" (the best) above, 9:96 / 14:291.]] As follows:

20326. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿for those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]﴾, that it is Paradise.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and those who did not respond to Him, [even] if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it﴾, He, Exalted is His mention, says: As for those who did not respond to God when He called them to His oneness (tawhid) and to acknowledging His lordship, and did not obey Him in what He commanded them, and did not follow His Messenger, confirming what he brought them from their Lord; [even] if they had all that is in the earth entirely, of any thing, and the like of it with it, as property belonging to them, and then that were accepted from them, and accepted from them as a substitute and an exchange for the punishment which God has prepared for them in the Fire of Hell, they would ransom themselves with it from it. God says: ﴿Those will have the worst accounting﴾, meaning: those who did not respond to God will have the worst accounting, that is, it is for them with God that He will take them to account for all their sins, so that He forgives them none of them, but punishes them for all of them. As follows:

20327. Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Awn narrated to us, from Farqad al-Sabakhi, who said: Shahr ibn Hawshab said to us: "﴿The worst accounting﴾ is that not even one thing of them is overlooked."
[[The report 20327: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah al-'Abdi al-Baghdadi, Tabari's teacher, trustworthy, previously mentioned under nos. 9373, 12851, 15766.
And Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Baghdadi, trustworthy, related from by the whole group (of compilers), previously mentioned under nos. 5090, 12549.
And "'Awn," apparently meaning 'Awn ibn Salam al-Qurashi al-Kufi, trustworthy, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib.
As for Farqad al-Sabakhi, he is Farqad ibn Ya'qub al-Sabakhi, Abu Ya'qub, who was weak and unreliable in narration, because he was not a man of hadith, and is not trustworthy. See his biography in al-Kabir 4/1/131, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/81, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:327.]]

20328. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Abi 'Uthman narrated to me, saying: Farqad al-Sabakhi narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "O Farqad, do you know what 'the worst accounting' is?" I said: "No." He said: "It is that a man is called to account for all his sins, and not one of them is forgiven him."
[[The report 20328: Farqad al-Sabakhi is not trustworthy, previously mentioned under no. 20327. This report will come again with another chain of narration, no. 20334.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾, He says: Their dwelling, in which they will dwell on the Day of Resurrection, is Hell. [[See the explanation of "al-ma'wa" (refuge) above, 15:26, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, He says: And wretched is the bed and the couch, Hell, which is their refuge on the Day of Resurrection. [[See the explanation of "al-mihad" (resting place) above, 12:435, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is then he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ ﴿It is only those of understanding (ulu al-albab) who take heed.﴾ (19)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, His remembrance, says: Is this one who knows that what Allah has sent down to you, O Muhammad, is the truth, so he believes in it, affirms it, and acts upon what is in it, like the one who is blind, who does not recognize the place of Allah's proof against him in it, nor know what obligations Allah has imposed upon him?

* *

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said in this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

20329- Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Is then he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, he said: These are a people who benefited from what they heard of the Book of Allah, understood it, and retained it. Allah said: ﴿like one who is blind﴾, he said: from the good, so he does not see it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is only those of understanding (ulu al-albab) who take heed﴾, it means: only those endowed with intellects are admonished by the signs of Allah and take lessons from them. [[See the explanation of "tadhakkur" in the earlier lexical indexes under (dh-k-r)]] "Al-albab" is the plural of "lubb" (kernel of the intellect, pure understanding). [[See the explanation of "al-albab" earlier: 3:383 / 4:162 / 5:580 / 6:211 / 11:97.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:** ﴿Those who fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the pact (20), and those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord and dread an evil reckoning (21).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, He says: Only those of understanding (ulu al-albab) take heed and learn from the signs of Allah, those who fulfil the injunction of Allah that He enjoined upon them [[See the explanation of "al-iifa'" (fulfilment) in the earlier lexical indexes under (w-f-y).]] ﴿and do not break the pact﴾, and do not violate the covenant that they made with Allah by acting contrary to it, doing other than what He commanded them and transgressing into what He forbade.

I have already explained the meaning of "al-ahd" (covenant) and "al-mithaq" (pact) earlier, with their evidences, so there is no need to repeat it here. [[See the explanation of "al-ahd" earlier, vol. 14, p. 141, note 1, and the sources cited there.
And the explanation of "al-mithaq" earlier, p. 208, note 1, and the sources cited there.]]

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

20330. A matter is only great by what Allah has made great, in the estimation of people of understanding and intellect, so magnify what Allah has magnified. Qatada said: It has been related to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say in his sermon: "There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾, Exalted is His mention, He says: And those who join the ties of kinship that Allah has commanded them to join, so they do not sever them [[See the explanation of "al-wasl" (joining) earlier, vol. 1, p. 415.]], ﴿and fear their Lord﴾, meaning: they fear Allah regarding severing them, lest they sever them, so that He punish them for severing them and for opposing His command concerning them.

What is in the printed edition seems better to me: "al-munaqasha".]]

20333. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and dread an evil reckoning﴾, he said: And what is "an evil reckoning"? He said: It is that in which there is no leniency. [[Al-jawaz: leniency and tolerance.]]

Commentary on the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who patiently persevere, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish the prayer (ṣalāh), and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good—those will have the good final attainment of the abode﴾ [13:22]

Abu Ja'far (al-Ṭabarī) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And those who are patient in fulfilling the covenant of Allah and in not breaking the pact and in maintaining the ties of kinship"= ﴿seeking the countenance of their Lord﴾. By His words ﴿seeking the countenance of their Lord﴾ He means: seeking to exalt Allah and to declare Him far above being opposed in His command, or doing something He dislikes, thereby disobeying Him= ﴿and establish the prayer﴾, meaning: they perform the obligatory prayer (ṣalāh) within its limits, at its appointed times= ﴿and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and openly﴾, meaning: they pay the obligatory alms-tax (zakāh) from their wealth, and spend from it in the ways in which Allah has commanded them to spend= ﴿secretly﴾ in privacy, ﴿and openly﴾ in public. As related:

20335 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿and establish the prayer﴾: he said, "It means the five prayers"= ﴿and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and openly﴾: he said, "It means the zakāh."

20336 – Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Patience" is steadfastness. He said: "Patience" in these two [senses]: patience for Allah in what He loves, even if it is burdensome to souls and bodies, and patience in refraining from what He dislikes, even if desires strive toward it. Whoever is like this is among the patient. And he recited: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final abode﴾ [13:24].

* *

As for His words ﴿and repel evil with good﴾, He means: they repel the harm of one who wrongs them among the people by doing good to him. [See the explanation of "al-darʾ" (repelling) previously: 2:22, 225 / 7:382.] As related:

20337 – Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and repel evil with good﴾: he said, "They repel evil with good; they do not requite evil with evil, but repel it with good."

* *

As for His words ﴿those will have the good final attainment of the abode﴾, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those whose attributes We have described, they are the ones for whom ﴿is the good final attainment of the abode﴾, meaning: they are the ones whom Allah has made to inherit the abode of the Gardens, in place of their abode which, had they not been believers, would have been theirs in the Fire; so Allah granted them this in place of that. [See the explanation of "al-ʿāqibah" (the final outcome) previously: 15:356, note 1, and the references there.]

It has also been said: the meaning of that is: those for whom, after their obedience to their Lord in this world, is the abode of the Gardens.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, and [also] whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
