Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 25:

The discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause corruption on the earth – those will have the curse, and for them is the evil home.﴾ (13:25)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His, the Exalted's, remembrance says: As for those who break the covenant of Allah, their breaking it is their opposition to the command of Allah and their acting in disobedience to Him [[See the explanation of "naqd" (breaking) in what has preceded: 9:363 / 10:125 / 14:22.]] ﴿after its ratification﴾, meaning: after they had bound themselves before Allah to act upon what He had enjoined upon them [[See the explanation of "mithaq" (covenant) in what has preceded, p. 419, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾, [[See the explanation of "wasl" (joining) in what has preceded, 1:415, and this work p. 420, footnote 1.]] meaning: and they sever the ties of kinship which Allah has commanded them to maintain = ﴿and cause corruption on the earth﴾, their corruption in it being their acting in disobedience to Allah ([[See the explanation of "corruption on the earth" in what has preceded in the indices of language (f-s-d).]] ﴿those will have the curse﴾), meaning: these will have the curse, which is distance from His mercy and exclusion from His gardens [[See the explanation of "la'nah" (curse) in what has preceded, 15:467, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿and for them is the evil home﴾, meaning: and for them is that which will distress them in the Hereafter.

* *

20349 – My father (ḥaddathanī) al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with Allah, because Allah says: ﴿And whoever associates with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 31], and breaking the covenant, and severing the ties of kinship, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those will have the curse, and for them is the evil home﴾. He means: the evil end.

20350 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His saying: ﴿and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾: It has reached us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If you do not walk to your kinsman on foot and do not give him from your wealth, then you have severed him."

20351 – Muḥammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, who said: I asked my father about this verse: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 103–104], "Are they the Ḥarūriyya?" He said: "No, but the Ḥarūriyya are those who ﴿break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause corruption on the earth – those will have the curse, and for them is the evil home﴾." And Saʿd used to call them the defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiqīn). [[Report 20351: Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqāş, a trustworthy Successor (tābiʿī) whom the compilers of the six books narrated from; he has passed several times, the last being no. 18776. It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Ṣaḥīḥ through Muḥammad ibn Bashshar, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, at length (Fath 8:323), and it will come at length in the tafsir 17:27 (Bulaq) in the commentary on the verse of Surah al-Kahf. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:370, through Ishaq, from Jarir, from Mansur, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, and said: "This is a ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Then see its takhrij in the unpublished books, in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:253. It will come with another isnad in the one that follows.]]

20352 – Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who said: I heard Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd say: I used to hold the codex (muṣḥaf) for Saʿd, and he came upon this verse, then he mentioned something similar to the ḥadīth of Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar. [[Report 20352: It is a repetition of the preceding one, from the narration of Abu Dawud al-Ṭayālisī, from Shuʿba.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 26:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the worldly life, but the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah widens provision for whomever of His creatures He wills, so He extends it to him from among them [[See the explanation of "extending" (al-basṭ) above, 5:288–290 / 10:452.]], because some of them would not be set right except by that. ﴿And restricts﴾ means: He straitens provision and livelihood for whomever of them He wills, so He constricts it for him, because nothing sets him right except restriction. ﴿And they rejoice in the worldly life﴾ means: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those to whom provision was extended in this world, despite their disbelief in Allah and their disobedience to Him, rejoice in what was extended to them in it, and they are ignorant of what is with Allah for the people of His obedience and of faith in Him in the Hereafter, of honour and delight.

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed of the measure of this worldly life compared with what is prepared for the people of faith in the Hereafter, and made His servants aware of its scantiness, saying: ﴿But the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment.﴾ He means: All that these people were given in this world of abundance, and of the provision extended to them in it and the ease of living, compared with what is with Allah for the people of His obedience in the Hereafter, ﴿is but a brief enjoyment﴾, a little and a worthless, passing thing. [[See the explanation of "enjoyment" (matā') above, p. 414, note 2, and the references there.]] As related:

20353 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Shababah related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿But a brief enjoyment﴾, he said: A little, passing thing.

20354 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid =

20355 - ... He said: And Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment﴾, he said: A little, passing thing.

20356 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabat regarding His words: ﴿And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment﴾, he said: Like the provision of a shepherd, which his family supplies him: a handful of dates, or a portion of flour, or something to drink milk with.

**On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿Those who disbelieve say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, God leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back (unabah)."﴾ (13:27)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The idolaters of your people say to you, O Muhammad: "Why has a sign not been sent down to you from your Lord, either an angel to be a warner with you, or a treasure to be cast down to you?" So say: "Indeed, God leaves astray whom He wills of you, O people," meaning He forsakes him, so that he does not affirm me or believe in what I have brought from my Lord. ﴿And guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, meaning he who returns in repentance from his disbelief and believes in Him. He grants him success in following me and affirming what I have brought from his Lord. The straying of those of you who go astray is not because no sign has been sent down to me from my Lord, nor is the guidance of those of you who are guided because a sign has been sent down to me. Rather, that is in the hand of God: He grants success to whomever of you He wills to believe, and forsakes whomever of you He wills, so that he does not believe.

* *

I have already explained the meaning of "inabah" (turning back in repentance) in more than one place in this book, with its evidences, which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See the explanation of "inabah" above, 15:406 and 454. Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him, forgot, for he did not mention "inabah" in any place other than these two nearby passages, and did not cite any evidence in explaining them. It seems that, as he went deep into the tafsir (exegesis), and had prepared his materials for it, the matter became confused for him, and he thought that what would come repeatedly had already passed repeatedly before, so he said here what he said, though a similar thing has already passed and I had pointed to it.]]

* *

2035 7- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾: that is, whoever repents and turns.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God. Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest. (28) Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy (ṭūbā) and a good return.﴾ (29)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And guides to Himself whoever turns back (in repentance)﴾, ﴿those who believe﴾.
* *
The phrase ﴿those who believe﴾ is in the accusative case, as a restatement of "man" (whoever), because "those who believe" are "whoever turns back," expressed as a rendering of it. [[The "tarjamah" (restatement) is either a substitution (badal) or an explanatory apposition (ʿatf al-bayān). See what preceded shortly at p. 423, note 1, and the references there.]]
* *
As for His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, He means: their hearts become calm and find comfort in the remembrance of God. [[See the explanation of "al-iṭmiʾnān" (tranquillity) earlier at 15:25, note 1, and the references there.]] As related:
20358. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, he said: their hearts became settled and at ease in the remembrance of God.
* *
As for His words: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, He means: surely in the remembrance of God the hearts of the believers become settled and at ease.  [[See the explanation of "al-iṭmiʾnān" earlier at 15:25, note 1, and the references there.]]
It has been said that by this He meant the hearts of the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).
Those who said this:
20359. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, that it refers to Muhammad and his Companions.
20360. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us [[This chain is repeated only in the printed edition, and the publisher of the first printed edition said: "So it is in the copies with this repetition, so look into it." It is not repeated in our manuscript, as though he did not refer back to it.]] =
20361. And al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: ʿAbd Allah told us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, he said: it refers to Muhammad and his Companions.
20362. ... He said: Ishaq told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, regarding His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, said: they are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).
* *
As for His words: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, "righteous deeds" are the good works, and that is acting upon what their Lord has commanded them. ﴿For them is joy (ṭūbā)﴾.
* *
The word "ṭūbā" (ṭūbā) is in the nominative case, governed by "lahum" (for them).
Some of the people of Basra and Kufa used to say: it is in the nominative, as one says in speech: "Woe (wayl) to ʿAmr."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The nominative case has been preferred for ﴿ṭūbā﴾ only because of the good form of its annexation without the preposition "lām", for one says "ṭūbāka" just as one says "waylaka" and "waybaka". Had it not been for the good form of its annexation without a "lām", the accusative would have been better and more eloquent, just as the accusative is better in their saying: "taʿsan li-Zayd, wa-buʿdan lahu wa-suḥqan" (ruin for Zayd, distance for him, and destruction), since annexation without "lām" is not good in these.
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) have differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾.
Some of them said: its meaning is: what an excellent thing is theirs.
Those who said this:
20363. Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Barawri, of the people of Kufa, told me, saying: Abu Zakariyya al-Kalbi told us, from ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ, who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about "ṭūbā lahum," and he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum" (what an excellent thing is theirs). [[Report 20363: "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Barawri, of the people of Kufa," the teacher of al-Tabari, is so written in the manuscript, and I do not know him. He was mentioned under number 9800, where I noted that I could not find him, and what preceded there was "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Marwazi," and I noted that he narrated from him in the History (Tarikh) 5:18. It is clear to me that he is the same person in all three places, because in the History he narrated: "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Kufi and ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib told me, both saying: Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Musʿab al-Kalbi told us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ told us." This is part of our present chain.
And "Abu Zakariyya al-Kalbi" is "Yahya ibn Musʿab al-Kalbi al-Kufi," who is "the neighbour of al-Aʿmash." He narrated stories from al-Aʿmash and narrated from ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ, and he is truthful (ṣadūq). He is biographed in al-Kabir 4/2/306 and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/190.
And "ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ al-Thaqafi" is one spoken of (mutakallam fīhi), mentioned shortly before under number 20229. In the manuscript here it was "ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ," and it is correct in the following chain in the manuscript; as for the printed edition, it followed the first error of the manuscript and left its second correction!!]]
20364. Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ told us, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum."
20365. Al-Harith told me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ told me, saying: I heard ʿIkrimah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum."
* *
Others said: its meaning is: happiness (ghibṭa) for them.
Those who said this:
20366. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: happiness for them.
20367. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
20368. ... He said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: joy and coolness of the eye (furaḥ wa-qurrat ʿayn).
Those who said this:
20369. ʿAli ibn Dawud and al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah told us, saying: Muʿawiyah told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he says: joy and coolness of the eye.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: the best (ḥusnā) for them.
Those who said this:
20370. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he says: the best for them, and it is a word from the speech of the Arabs.
20371. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, this is an Arabic word; a man says: "ṭūbā laka," meaning: you have attained good.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: good for them.
Those who said this:
20372. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: good for them.
20373. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the good and the honour which God has given them.
* *
Others said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾ is the name of one of the names of Paradise, and the meaning of the statement is: Paradise is theirs.
Those who said this:
20374. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the name of Paradise, in Abyssinian.
20375. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the name of the land of Paradise, in Abyssinian.
20376. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Mashjuj, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "ṭūbā" is the name of Paradise in Indian (Hindi).
20377. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Dawud ibn Mihran told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Saʿid ibn Mashjuj, who said: the name of Paradise in Indian is: "ṭūbā." [[Reports 20376 and 20377: "Saʿid ibn Mashjuj," or "ibn Masjuh," or "ibn Masjuʿ," is so written differently in the manuscript, and then in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:523, and al-Durr al-Manthur 4:59, where it is attributed to Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh. I did not find any mention of him in any book of the biographers, even after checking for the various forms of scribal error and distortion.
But I found in Lisan al-ʿArab, under the roots (karam) and (kasa), where it says: "Saʿid ibn Masḥuh al-Shaybani," and in the commentary on the Qamus: "Ibn Mashjuj," and al-Sirafi and Ibn Burri attributed to him the poetry of Abu Khalid al-Qanani al-Kharijī, which begins: "Indeed my daughters have increased life in my sight with love, for they are among the weak." See al-Kamil 2:107. This is the furthest I found, and I do not know what connection there is between these two names, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.]]
20378. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-Suddi, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
20379. ... He said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
20380. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
20381. Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy and a good return﴾, he said: When God created Paradise and finished it, He said: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy and a good return﴾, and that was when it pleased Him.
20382. Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: Sharik told us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
* *
Others said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾ is a tree in Paradise.
Those who said this:
20383. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid told us, from Musa ibn Salim, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, a tree in Paradise. [[Report 20383: "Musa ibn Salim," client of the family of al-ʿAbbas, is trustworthy (thiqa). His narration from Ibn ʿAbbas is mursal (with a missing link), and he narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbbas. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/284, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/143.]]
20384. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾: a tree in Paradise, to which He says: "Split open (tafattaqī) for My servant whatever he wishes!" So it splits open for him, bringing forth horses with their saddles and bridles, and camels with their halters, and whatever clothing he wishes. [[Report 20384: "al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Jabir al-Hadani al-Hamli," the blind, who is ascribed to his grandfather so it is said: "al-Ashʿath ibn Jabir." He is trustworthy, and his narrations are considered. al-ʿUqayli said: there is error in his narration. Ibn Maʿin, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy. He passed as number 8358, and he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/429 under "al-Ashʿath ibn Jabir," then in it 1/1/433 under "al-Ashʿath Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hamli," and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/273.
And "Shahr ibn Hawshab" passed many times; they declared him trustworthy and spoke of him.
This report is a mawquf report (ending with Abu Hurayrah). It will come by another route as number 20386.]]
20385. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "ṭūbā" is a tree in Paradise; every tree of Paradise is from it, its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise.
20386. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree called "ṭūbā," and God says to it: "Split open!" = and he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla from Ibn Thawr. [[Report 20386: it is a repetition of the report that passed as number 20384.]]
20387. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Marwan told us, saying: al-ʿAlaʾ informed us, from Shammar ibn ʿAtiyyah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: it is a tree in Paradise called "ṭūbā."
20388. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Hassan Abu al-Ashras, from Mughith ibn Sumayy, who said: "ṭūbā" is a tree in Paradise. There is no dwelling in Paradise without a branch of it in it; the bird comes and lands, and it calls to it, and it eats from one side of it cooked meat and from the other side roasted meat, then it says: "Fly!" and it flies. [[Report 20388: "Mansur" is "Mansur ibn al-Muʿtamir," who passed many times.
And "Hassan Abu al-Ashras" is "Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras ibn ʿAmmar al-Kahili," and he is "Hassan ibn al-Mundhir," his kunya and his father's kunya being "Abu al-Ashras." He is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/32, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/235.
And "Mughith ibn Sumayy al-Awzaʿi" is a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi), biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/24, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/391.
This report will come at length by another chain as number 20392.]]
20389. ... He said: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiyah told me, from some people of Syria, who said: Indeed your Lord took a pearl and placed it on His palms, then He shaped it between His two hands, then He planted it in the middle of the people of Paradise, then He said to it: "Extend until you reach My pleasure." So it did, and when it became straight, the rivers of Paradise gushed forth from its roots, and it is "ṭūbā."

٢٠٣٩٠- Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb say: "In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba. A rider would travel in its shade for a hundred years without crossing it. Its blossoms are *riyat* [[*Al-riyat* is the plural of *rayta*, which is any soft, thin garment.]] and its leaves are *burud* [[*Burud* is the plural of *burd*, a kind of embroidered garment.]]. Its branches are ambergris, its valley is hyacinth, its soil is camphor, and its mud is musk. From its root flow rivers of wine, milk and honey, and it is a gathering place for the people of Paradise. While they are in their gathering, angels come to them from their Lord, leading she-camels bridled with chains of gold. Their faces are like lamps for their beauty, and their hair is as soft as *kharr al-mir'izzi* [[*Al-mir'izzi* (with a kasra on the mim, a sukun on the ra, and a kasra on the ayn with a shadda on the zay) is the down beneath the hair of a goat, the softest of wool. The mim in *al-mir'izzi* is extra, and its root is (r-‘-z).]] in its softness. On them are saddles whose boards are of hyacinth, their stirrups are of gold, and their garments are of silk brocade and thick silk. They make them kneel and say: 'Our Lord has sent us to you so that you may visit Him and greet Him.'" He said: "They mount them. It is swifter than a bird and softer-footed than a bed, camels that need no servant. A man walks beside his brother, speaking with him and conversing privately. The ear of one riding camel does not strike the ear of its companion, nor does the kneeling of one camel touch the kneeling of its companion [[This is as written in the manuscript. In Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* it reads *barak*, and in *al-Durr al-Manthur* it reads *la tazill rahila bizill sahibatiha* ("one riding camel does not slip with the slipping of its companion"). I incline to think the correct reading is *wa la warak rahila warak sahibatiha* ("nor does the thigh of one riding camel touch the thigh of its companion"), but the first copyist joined the waw to the ra, so our copyist joined them too, without clarity or knowledge.]], so much so that the tree moves aside from their path, lest it separate a man from his brother." He said: "They come to the Merciful, the Compassionate, and He unveils for them His noble face so that they may look upon Him. When they see Him they say: 'O God, You are peace, and from You is peace, and to You belong majesty and honour.'" He said: "Then, blessed and exalted is He, says: 'I am peace, and from Me is peace, and upon you has My mercy and My love been decreed. Welcome, My servants who feared Me unseen and obeyed My command.'" He said: "They say: 'Our Lord, we have not worshipped You as You deserve, nor have we esteemed You as You deserve. So permit us to prostrate before You.'" He said: "God says: 'It is not a place of toil or worship, but a dwelling of dominion and bliss, and I have lifted from you the toil of worship. So ask Me for whatever you wish, for each one of you has his wish.'" They ask Him, until the one with the humblest wish says: 'My Lord, the people of the world competed in their worldly life and were constrained therein. My Lord, give me everything they had from the day You created it until the world ended.'" God says: "Your wish has fallen short for you today, and you have asked less than your rank. This is yours from Me, and I will honour you with My station, for in My giving there is no grudging and no withholding [[In the printed edition it reads *wa la qasr yad* ("nor shortness of hand"), which is a feeble statement, indeed the very epitome of feebleness. *Al-tasrid* in giving means reducing it.]]." He said: "Then He says: 'Present to My servants what their wishes have not reached and what has not occurred to them.'" He said: "They present to them, until they fulfil the wishes that are in their souls. Among what they present to them are harnessed thoroughbred steeds, each four of which have a throne of a single ruby, and on each throne a dome of poured gold, and in each dome Paradise couches spread out, and in each dome two maidens of the wide-eyed houris, and on each maiden two garments of the garments of Paradise. There is no colour in Paradise except that it is in them both, and no fragrant scent except that they are both perfumed with it. The light of their faces penetrates the thickness of the dome, so that whoever sees them thinks they are beyond the dome. Their marrow is seen from above their shins like a white thread within a red ruby. He sees in them such excellence over his companion as the excellence of the sun over the stones, or greater, and their excellence over him is like that. Then he enters to them, and they greet him, kiss him and embrace him, and say to him: 'By God, we did not think that God would create the likes of you.' Then God commands the angels, and they lead them in a row through Paradise, until each man reaches the station prepared for him."
[[Athar (report) 20390: Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah al-Baghdadi, a shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy; he has passed as no. 2252, 3958.
And Isma'il ibn al-Karim ibn Ma'qil al-San'ani, trustworthy; he has passed as no. 995, 5598.
And Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, trustworthy; he narrated from his paternal uncle Wahb ibn Munabbih; he has passed as no. 995.
Ibn Kathir has narrated it in his *Tafsir* (4:524), and he said before it: "Ibn Jarir narrated here from Wahb ibn Munabbih a strange and wondrous report," then he completed the report through the route of Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: "This wording is strange, and the report is wondrous, and some of it has corroborating reports."]]

٢٠٣٩١- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Hammad, who said: "There is a tree in Paradise, and in the house of every believer is a branch of it."

٢٠٣٩٢- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras, from Mughith ibn Sumayy, who said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise. If a man were to ride a young she-camel, a *jadha'*, or a young female camel, and travel around with it, he would not reach the place from which he set out until he died of old age. There is no dwelling of the people of Paradise without a branch of that tree hanging over them. When they wish to eat from its fruit, it bends down to them, and they eat from it as much as they wish. Birds come and eat from it, both dried and roasted, as much as they wish, and then fly away."
[[Athar 20392: Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras, passed as no. 20388. And Mughith ibn Sumayy, passed as no. 20388.
It is the lengthier form of the earlier report, no. 20388.]]

* *

It has been narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) a report similar to what those who say it is a tree have said.
Mention of the narration to that effect:

٢٠٣٩٣- Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Qumsi narrated to me, saying: Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salam narrated to us, from Zayd, that he heard Abu Salam say: Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali narrated to us, that he heard Utba ibn Abd al-Sulami say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes. In it is a tree called Tuba; it corresponds to Firdaws." He said: "What tree of our land does it resemble?" He said: "It does not resemble any tree of your land. But have you come to Syria?" He said: "No, O Messenger of God." He said: "It resembles a tree called the *jawza* (walnut), which grows on a single trunk, then its top spreads out." He said: "How great is its root?" He said: "If you were to travel with a young camel of your people's herd, it would not go around its root until its collarbones were broken from old age [[Athar 20393: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Qumsi, a shaykh of al-Tabari; I have found no biography of him in the books available to me. Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', trustworthy, passed as no. 3833. Mu'awiya ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam, trustworthy, the group narrated from him; he narrated from his father, his grandfather, and his brother Zayd; passed as no. 16557.
His brother Zayd ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam, trustworthy, narrated from his grandfather Abu Salam; he is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Kabir* 2/1/361, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/564.
Abu Salam is Mamtur al-Aswad al-Habashi, trustworthy, passed several times, the last being no. 16557.
Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, a Successor, trustworthy, mentioned in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/320.
Utba ibn Abd al-Sulami, Abu al-Walid, a Companion who narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ); mentioned in *al-Isaba*, *Usd al-Ghaba*, *al-Istiab*, *al-Tahdhib*, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/371, and Ibn Sa'd 7/2/132.
This is a good isnad. Ahmad narrated it in his *Musnad* (4:183, 184), in full, through the route of Ali ibn Bahr, from Hisham ibn Yusuf, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali. This isnad is also sound, and Ibn al-Qayyim quoted it from the *Musnad* in *Hadi al-Arwah* (1:263, 264).]]

٢٠٣٩٤- Al-Hasan ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: ﴿Good fortune is theirs, and a good place of return﴾: It is a tree which God planted with His own hand, and into which He breathed of His spirit. It grew with ornaments and garments [[In the printed edition the word "grew" (nabatat) is omitted; I have restored it from the manuscript.]], and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise.
[[Athar 20394: Al-Hasan ibn Shabib ibn Rashid, a shaykh of al-Tabari, passed as nos. 9642, 11383. Ibn Adi said: "He narrated from the trustworthy things that are falsehoods, and he connected reports that are *mursal*" (a report in which the chain is broken at the Companion level).
And Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari: perhaps he is al-Raqqi, since al-Raqqa is counted from al-Jazira. He is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Yashkuri al-Tahhan, al-Maymun al-Raqqi, a wicked liar who fabricates hadith; he narrated fabricated reports from his shaykh al-Maymun ibn Mihran and others. He is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib*, *Tarikh Baghdad* 5:279, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/258, and *Mizan al-I'tidal* 3:60. In the printed edition it reads "al-Jaziri" (al-Jaziri), different from the manuscript.
Furat ibn Abi al-Furat: Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Truthful, there is no harm in him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: "He was upright in conduct and in narrations." Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him, but Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Ibn Adi said: "Weakness is evident in his narrations." Al-Saji said: "Weak; he narrates hadith with some munkar (rejected) reports." He is mentioned in *al-Kabir* 4/1/129, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/80, *Mizan al-I'tidal* 2:316, and *Lisan al-Mizan* 4:432.
Mu'awiya ibn Iyas al-Muzani, a trustworthy Successor, passed as nos. 11211, 11409. His father Qurra ibn Iyas ibn Hilal ibn Ri'ab al-Muzani has companionship; he is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib* and *al-Kabir* 4/1/180.
This report has a completely destroyed isnad, and it suffices that there is in it the matter of Muhammad ibn Ziyad. I have not found it except in al-Tabari.]]

٢٠٣٩٥- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Darraj told him that Abu al-Haytham told him, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: A man said to him: "O Messenger of God, what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, a hundred years' journey, from whose sheaths the garments of the people of Paradise emerge."
[[Athar 20395: Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Ansari al-Misri, trustworthy, the group narrated from him, passed several times, the last being no. 17429.
Darraj is Darraj ibn Sam'an, Abu al-Simh, one spoken of (critically), passed several times, the last being no. 17754.
Abu al-Haytham is Sulayman ibn Amr al-Atawari al-Misri, trustworthy, passed as nos. 1387, 5518.
A similar isnad has passed as no. 1387, and my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad (may God have mercy on him) authenticated this isnad. Ibn Adi quoted from Ahmad ibn Hanbal: "The reports of Darraj from Abu al-Haytham from Abu Sa'id contain weakness." Ibn Shahin said: "Whatever is in this isnad is not objectionable." Ahmad's judgement on Darraj is severe, for Abd Allah ibn Ahmad quoted from him: "His hadith is munkar." In my view, authenticating an isnad like this involves some rashness, and its best state is that it is among what is not objectionable and may be taken as a supporting report.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* (3:71) through Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj Abu al-Simh. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated it in his *Tarikh* (4:91), through Asad ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a, at greater length, its opening being: "A man said to him: 'O Messenger of God, Tuba to whoever saw you and believed in you!' He said: 'Tuba to whoever saw me and believed in me; then Tuba, then Tuba, then Tuba to whoever believed in me without seeing me.' A man said to him: 'And what is Tuba?'" — the hadith continues.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Upon this interpretation which we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the transmission of it, it must be that the statement regarding the nominative case of God's words ﴿Good fortune is theirs﴾ is contrary to the view we related from the grammarians concerning it. This is because the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is that *Tuba* is the name of a tree in Paradise. Given that this is so, it is a proper noun, like Zayd and Amr. And when that is so, the words ﴿and a good place of return﴾ can only be in the nominative case, being conjoined to *Tuba*.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a good place of return﴾, He means: and a good place of return (*munqalab*) [[See the explanation of *al-ma'ab* earlier, 6:258, 259.]], as follows:

٢٠٣٩٦- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿and a good place of return﴾, that he said: "A good place of return."
[[See the explanation of *al-ma'ab* earlier, 6:258, 259.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God. Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest. (28) Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy (ṭūbā) and a good return.﴾ (29)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And guides to Himself whoever turns back (in repentance)﴾, ﴿those who believe﴾.
* *
The phrase ﴿those who believe﴾ is in the accusative case, as a restatement of "man" (whoever), because "those who believe" are "whoever turns back," expressed as a rendering of it. [[The "tarjamah" (restatement) is either a substitution (badal) or an explanatory apposition (ʿatf al-bayān). See what preceded shortly at p. 423, note 1, and the references there.]]
* *
As for His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, He means: their hearts become calm and find comfort in the remembrance of God. [[See the explanation of "al-iṭmiʾnān" (tranquillity) earlier at 15:25, note 1, and the references there.]] As related:
20358. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, he said: their hearts became settled and at ease in the remembrance of God.
* *
As for His words: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, He means: surely in the remembrance of God the hearts of the believers become settled and at ease.  [[See the explanation of "al-iṭmiʾnān" earlier at 15:25, note 1, and the references there.]]
It has been said that by this He meant the hearts of the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).
Those who said this:
20359. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, that it refers to Muhammad and his Companions.
20360. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us [[This chain is repeated only in the printed edition, and the publisher of the first printed edition said: "So it is in the copies with this repetition, so look into it." It is not repeated in our manuscript, as though he did not refer back to it.]] =
20361. And al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: ʿAbd Allah told us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾, he said: it refers to Muhammad and his Companions.
20362. ... He said: Ishaq told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, regarding His words: ﴿and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God﴾, said: they are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).
* *
As for His words: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, "righteous deeds" are the good works, and that is acting upon what their Lord has commanded them. ﴿For them is joy (ṭūbā)﴾.
* *
The word "ṭūbā" (ṭūbā) is in the nominative case, governed by "lahum" (for them).
Some of the people of Basra and Kufa used to say: it is in the nominative, as one says in speech: "Woe (wayl) to ʿAmr."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The nominative case has been preferred for ﴿ṭūbā﴾ only because of the good form of its annexation without the preposition "lām", for one says "ṭūbāka" just as one says "waylaka" and "waybaka". Had it not been for the good form of its annexation without a "lām", the accusative would have been better and more eloquent, just as the accusative is better in their saying: "taʿsan li-Zayd, wa-buʿdan lahu wa-suḥqan" (ruin for Zayd, distance for him, and destruction), since annexation without "lām" is not good in these.
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) have differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾.
Some of them said: its meaning is: what an excellent thing is theirs.
Those who said this:
20363. Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Barawri, of the people of Kufa, told me, saying: Abu Zakariyya al-Kalbi told us, from ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ, who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about "ṭūbā lahum," and he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum" (what an excellent thing is theirs). [[Report 20363: "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Barawri, of the people of Kufa," the teacher of al-Tabari, is so written in the manuscript, and I do not know him. He was mentioned under number 9800, where I noted that I could not find him, and what preceded there was "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Marwazi," and I noted that he narrated from him in the History (Tarikh) 5:18. It is clear to me that he is the same person in all three places, because in the History he narrated: "Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Kufi and ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib told me, both saying: Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Musʿab al-Kalbi told us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ told us." This is part of our present chain.
And "Abu Zakariyya al-Kalbi" is "Yahya ibn Musʿab al-Kalbi al-Kufi," who is "the neighbour of al-Aʿmash." He narrated stories from al-Aʿmash and narrated from ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ, and he is truthful (ṣadūq). He is biographed in al-Kabir 4/2/306 and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/190.
And "ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ al-Thaqafi" is one spoken of (mutakallam fīhi), mentioned shortly before under number 20229. In the manuscript here it was "ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ," and it is correct in the following chain in the manuscript; as for the printed edition, it followed the first error of the manuscript and left its second correction!!]]
20364. Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ told us, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum."
20365. Al-Harith told me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Nafiʿ told me, saying: I heard ʿIkrimah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "Nuʿma mā lahum."
* *
Others said: its meaning is: happiness (ghibṭa) for them.
Those who said this:
20366. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: happiness for them.
20367. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
20368. ... He said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: joy and coolness of the eye (furaḥ wa-qurrat ʿayn).
Those who said this:
20369. ʿAli ibn Dawud and al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah told us, saying: Muʿawiyah told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he says: joy and coolness of the eye.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: the best (ḥusnā) for them.
Those who said this:
20370. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he says: the best for them, and it is a word from the speech of the Arabs.
20371. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, this is an Arabic word; a man says: "ṭūbā laka," meaning: you have attained good.
* *
Others said: its meaning is: good for them.
Those who said this:
20372. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: good for them.
20373. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the good and the honour which God has given them.
* *
Others said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾ is the name of one of the names of Paradise, and the meaning of the statement is: Paradise is theirs.
Those who said this:
20374. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the name of Paradise, in Abyssinian.
20375. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: the name of the land of Paradise, in Abyssinian.
20376. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Mashjuj, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: "ṭūbā" is the name of Paradise in Indian (Hindi).
20377. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Dawud ibn Mihran told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Saʿid ibn Mashjuj, who said: the name of Paradise in Indian is: "ṭūbā." [[Reports 20376 and 20377: "Saʿid ibn Mashjuj," or "ibn Masjuh," or "ibn Masjuʿ," is so written differently in the manuscript, and then in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:523, and al-Durr al-Manthur 4:59, where it is attributed to Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh. I did not find any mention of him in any book of the biographers, even after checking for the various forms of scribal error and distortion.
But I found in Lisan al-ʿArab, under the roots (karam) and (kasa), where it says: "Saʿid ibn Masḥuh al-Shaybani," and in the commentary on the Qamus: "Ibn Mashjuj," and al-Sirafi and Ibn Burri attributed to him the poetry of Abu Khalid al-Qanani al-Kharijī, which begins: "Indeed my daughters have increased life in my sight with love, for they are among the weak." See al-Kamil 2:107. This is the furthest I found, and I do not know what connection there is between these two names, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.]]
20378. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-Suddi, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
20379. ... He said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
20380. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
20381. Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy and a good return﴾, he said: When God created Paradise and finished it, He said: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is joy and a good return﴾, and that was when it pleased Him.
20382. Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: Sharik told us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: Paradise.
* *
Others said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾ is a tree in Paradise.
Those who said this:
20383. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid told us, from Musa ibn Salim, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, a tree in Paradise. [[Report 20383: "Musa ibn Salim," client of the family of al-ʿAbbas, is trustworthy (thiqa). His narration from Ibn ʿAbbas is mursal (with a missing link), and he narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbbas. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/284, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/143.]]
20384. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾: a tree in Paradise, to which He says: "Split open (tafattaqī) for My servant whatever he wishes!" So it splits open for him, bringing forth horses with their saddles and bridles, and camels with their halters, and whatever clothing he wishes. [[Report 20384: "al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Jabir al-Hadani al-Hamli," the blind, who is ascribed to his grandfather so it is said: "al-Ashʿath ibn Jabir." He is trustworthy, and his narrations are considered. al-ʿUqayli said: there is error in his narration. Ibn Maʿin, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy. He passed as number 8358, and he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/429 under "al-Ashʿath ibn Jabir," then in it 1/1/433 under "al-Ashʿath Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hamli," and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/273.
And "Shahr ibn Hawshab" passed many times; they declared him trustworthy and spoke of him.
This report is a mawquf report (ending with Abu Hurayrah). It will come by another route as number 20386.]]
20385. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Jaʿfar, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "ṭūbā" is a tree in Paradise; every tree of Paradise is from it, its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise.
20386. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree called "ṭūbā," and God says to it: "Split open!" = and he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla from Ibn Thawr. [[Report 20386: it is a repetition of the report that passed as number 20384.]]
20387. Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Marwan told us, saying: al-ʿAlaʾ informed us, from Shammar ibn ʿAtiyyah, regarding His words: ﴿ṭūbā lahum﴾, he said: it is a tree in Paradise called "ṭūbā."
20388. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Hassan Abu al-Ashras, from Mughith ibn Sumayy, who said: "ṭūbā" is a tree in Paradise. There is no dwelling in Paradise without a branch of it in it; the bird comes and lands, and it calls to it, and it eats from one side of it cooked meat and from the other side roasted meat, then it says: "Fly!" and it flies. [[Report 20388: "Mansur" is "Mansur ibn al-Muʿtamir," who passed many times.
And "Hassan Abu al-Ashras" is "Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras ibn ʿAmmar al-Kahili," and he is "Hassan ibn al-Mundhir," his kunya and his father's kunya being "Abu al-Ashras." He is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/32, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/235.
And "Mughith ibn Sumayy al-Awzaʿi" is a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi), biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/24, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/391.
This report will come at length by another chain as number 20392.]]
20389. ... He said: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiyah told me, from some people of Syria, who said: Indeed your Lord took a pearl and placed it on His palms, then He shaped it between His two hands, then He planted it in the middle of the people of Paradise, then He said to it: "Extend until you reach My pleasure." So it did, and when it became straight, the rivers of Paradise gushed forth from its roots, and it is "ṭūbā."

٢٠٣٩٠- Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb say: "In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba. A rider would travel in its shade for a hundred years without crossing it. Its blossoms are *riyat* [[*Al-riyat* is the plural of *rayta*, which is any soft, thin garment.]] and its leaves are *burud* [[*Burud* is the plural of *burd*, a kind of embroidered garment.]]. Its branches are ambergris, its valley is hyacinth, its soil is camphor, and its mud is musk. From its root flow rivers of wine, milk and honey, and it is a gathering place for the people of Paradise. While they are in their gathering, angels come to them from their Lord, leading she-camels bridled with chains of gold. Their faces are like lamps for their beauty, and their hair is as soft as *kharr al-mir'izzi* [[*Al-mir'izzi* (with a kasra on the mim, a sukun on the ra, and a kasra on the ayn with a shadda on the zay) is the down beneath the hair of a goat, the softest of wool. The mim in *al-mir'izzi* is extra, and its root is (r-‘-z).]] in its softness. On them are saddles whose boards are of hyacinth, their stirrups are of gold, and their garments are of silk brocade and thick silk. They make them kneel and say: 'Our Lord has sent us to you so that you may visit Him and greet Him.'" He said: "They mount them. It is swifter than a bird and softer-footed than a bed, camels that need no servant. A man walks beside his brother, speaking with him and conversing privately. The ear of one riding camel does not strike the ear of its companion, nor does the kneeling of one camel touch the kneeling of its companion [[This is as written in the manuscript. In Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* it reads *barak*, and in *al-Durr al-Manthur* it reads *la tazill rahila bizill sahibatiha* ("one riding camel does not slip with the slipping of its companion"). I incline to think the correct reading is *wa la warak rahila warak sahibatiha* ("nor does the thigh of one riding camel touch the thigh of its companion"), but the first copyist joined the waw to the ra, so our copyist joined them too, without clarity or knowledge.]], so much so that the tree moves aside from their path, lest it separate a man from his brother." He said: "They come to the Merciful, the Compassionate, and He unveils for them His noble face so that they may look upon Him. When they see Him they say: 'O God, You are peace, and from You is peace, and to You belong majesty and honour.'" He said: "Then, blessed and exalted is He, says: 'I am peace, and from Me is peace, and upon you has My mercy and My love been decreed. Welcome, My servants who feared Me unseen and obeyed My command.'" He said: "They say: 'Our Lord, we have not worshipped You as You deserve, nor have we esteemed You as You deserve. So permit us to prostrate before You.'" He said: "God says: 'It is not a place of toil or worship, but a dwelling of dominion and bliss, and I have lifted from you the toil of worship. So ask Me for whatever you wish, for each one of you has his wish.'" They ask Him, until the one with the humblest wish says: 'My Lord, the people of the world competed in their worldly life and were constrained therein. My Lord, give me everything they had from the day You created it until the world ended.'" God says: "Your wish has fallen short for you today, and you have asked less than your rank. This is yours from Me, and I will honour you with My station, for in My giving there is no grudging and no withholding [[In the printed edition it reads *wa la qasr yad* ("nor shortness of hand"), which is a feeble statement, indeed the very epitome of feebleness. *Al-tasrid* in giving means reducing it.]]." He said: "Then He says: 'Present to My servants what their wishes have not reached and what has not occurred to them.'" He said: "They present to them, until they fulfil the wishes that are in their souls. Among what they present to them are harnessed thoroughbred steeds, each four of which have a throne of a single ruby, and on each throne a dome of poured gold, and in each dome Paradise couches spread out, and in each dome two maidens of the wide-eyed houris, and on each maiden two garments of the garments of Paradise. There is no colour in Paradise except that it is in them both, and no fragrant scent except that they are both perfumed with it. The light of their faces penetrates the thickness of the dome, so that whoever sees them thinks they are beyond the dome. Their marrow is seen from above their shins like a white thread within a red ruby. He sees in them such excellence over his companion as the excellence of the sun over the stones, or greater, and their excellence over him is like that. Then he enters to them, and they greet him, kiss him and embrace him, and say to him: 'By God, we did not think that God would create the likes of you.' Then God commands the angels, and they lead them in a row through Paradise, until each man reaches the station prepared for him."
[[Athar (report) 20390: Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah al-Baghdadi, a shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy; he has passed as no. 2252, 3958.
And Isma'il ibn al-Karim ibn Ma'qil al-San'ani, trustworthy; he has passed as no. 995, 5598.
And Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, trustworthy; he narrated from his paternal uncle Wahb ibn Munabbih; he has passed as no. 995.
Ibn Kathir has narrated it in his *Tafsir* (4:524), and he said before it: "Ibn Jarir narrated here from Wahb ibn Munabbih a strange and wondrous report," then he completed the report through the route of Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: "This wording is strange, and the report is wondrous, and some of it has corroborating reports."]]

٢٠٣٩١- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Hammad, who said: "There is a tree in Paradise, and in the house of every believer is a branch of it."

٢٠٣٩٢- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras, from Mughith ibn Sumayy, who said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise. If a man were to ride a young she-camel, a *jadha'*, or a young female camel, and travel around with it, he would not reach the place from which he set out until he died of old age. There is no dwelling of the people of Paradise without a branch of that tree hanging over them. When they wish to eat from its fruit, it bends down to them, and they eat from it as much as they wish. Birds come and eat from it, both dried and roasted, as much as they wish, and then fly away."
[[Athar 20392: Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras, passed as no. 20388. And Mughith ibn Sumayy, passed as no. 20388.
It is the lengthier form of the earlier report, no. 20388.]]

* *

It has been narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) a report similar to what those who say it is a tree have said.
Mention of the narration to that effect:

٢٠٣٩٣- Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Qumsi narrated to me, saying: Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salam narrated to us, from Zayd, that he heard Abu Salam say: Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali narrated to us, that he heard Utba ibn Abd al-Sulami say: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes. In it is a tree called Tuba; it corresponds to Firdaws." He said: "What tree of our land does it resemble?" He said: "It does not resemble any tree of your land. But have you come to Syria?" He said: "No, O Messenger of God." He said: "It resembles a tree called the *jawza* (walnut), which grows on a single trunk, then its top spreads out." He said: "How great is its root?" He said: "If you were to travel with a young camel of your people's herd, it would not go around its root until its collarbones were broken from old age [[Athar 20393: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Qumsi, a shaykh of al-Tabari; I have found no biography of him in the books available to me. Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', trustworthy, passed as no. 3833. Mu'awiya ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam, trustworthy, the group narrated from him; he narrated from his father, his grandfather, and his brother Zayd; passed as no. 16557.
His brother Zayd ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam, trustworthy, narrated from his grandfather Abu Salam; he is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Kabir* 2/1/361, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/564.
Abu Salam is Mamtur al-Aswad al-Habashi, trustworthy, passed several times, the last being no. 16557.
Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, a Successor, trustworthy, mentioned in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/320.
Utba ibn Abd al-Sulami, Abu al-Walid, a Companion who narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ); mentioned in *al-Isaba*, *Usd al-Ghaba*, *al-Istiab*, *al-Tahdhib*, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/371, and Ibn Sa'd 7/2/132.
This is a good isnad. Ahmad narrated it in his *Musnad* (4:183, 184), in full, through the route of Ali ibn Bahr, from Hisham ibn Yusuf, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali. This isnad is also sound, and Ibn al-Qayyim quoted it from the *Musnad* in *Hadi al-Arwah* (1:263, 264).]]

٢٠٣٩٤- Al-Hasan ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari narrated to us, from Furat ibn Abi al-Furat, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: ﴿Good fortune is theirs, and a good place of return﴾: It is a tree which God planted with His own hand, and into which He breathed of His spirit. It grew with ornaments and garments [[In the printed edition the word "grew" (nabatat) is omitted; I have restored it from the manuscript.]], and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise.
[[Athar 20394: Al-Hasan ibn Shabib ibn Rashid, a shaykh of al-Tabari, passed as nos. 9642, 11383. Ibn Adi said: "He narrated from the trustworthy things that are falsehoods, and he connected reports that are *mursal*" (a report in which the chain is broken at the Companion level).
And Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Jazari: perhaps he is al-Raqqi, since al-Raqqa is counted from al-Jazira. He is Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Yashkuri al-Tahhan, al-Maymun al-Raqqi, a wicked liar who fabricates hadith; he narrated fabricated reports from his shaykh al-Maymun ibn Mihran and others. He is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib*, *Tarikh Baghdad* 5:279, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/258, and *Mizan al-I'tidal* 3:60. In the printed edition it reads "al-Jaziri" (al-Jaziri), different from the manuscript.
Furat ibn Abi al-Furat: Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Truthful, there is no harm in him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: "He was upright in conduct and in narrations." Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him, but Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Ibn Adi said: "Weakness is evident in his narrations." Al-Saji said: "Weak; he narrates hadith with some munkar (rejected) reports." He is mentioned in *al-Kabir* 4/1/129, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/80, *Mizan al-I'tidal* 2:316, and *Lisan al-Mizan* 4:432.
Mu'awiya ibn Iyas al-Muzani, a trustworthy Successor, passed as nos. 11211, 11409. His father Qurra ibn Iyas ibn Hilal ibn Ri'ab al-Muzani has companionship; he is mentioned in *al-Tahdhib* and *al-Kabir* 4/1/180.
This report has a completely destroyed isnad, and it suffices that there is in it the matter of Muhammad ibn Ziyad. I have not found it except in al-Tabari.]]

٢٠٣٩٥- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Darraj told him that Abu al-Haytham told him, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: A man said to him: "O Messenger of God, what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, a hundred years' journey, from whose sheaths the garments of the people of Paradise emerge."
[[Athar 20395: Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Ansari al-Misri, trustworthy, the group narrated from him, passed several times, the last being no. 17429.
Darraj is Darraj ibn Sam'an, Abu al-Simh, one spoken of (critically), passed several times, the last being no. 17754.
Abu al-Haytham is Sulayman ibn Amr al-Atawari al-Misri, trustworthy, passed as nos. 1387, 5518.
A similar isnad has passed as no. 1387, and my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad (may God have mercy on him) authenticated this isnad. Ibn Adi quoted from Ahmad ibn Hanbal: "The reports of Darraj from Abu al-Haytham from Abu Sa'id contain weakness." Ibn Shahin said: "Whatever is in this isnad is not objectionable." Ahmad's judgement on Darraj is severe, for Abd Allah ibn Ahmad quoted from him: "His hadith is munkar." In my view, authenticating an isnad like this involves some rashness, and its best state is that it is among what is not objectionable and may be taken as a supporting report.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* (3:71) through Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj Abu al-Simh. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi narrated it in his *Tarikh* (4:91), through Asad ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a, at greater length, its opening being: "A man said to him: 'O Messenger of God, Tuba to whoever saw you and believed in you!' He said: 'Tuba to whoever saw me and believed in me; then Tuba, then Tuba, then Tuba to whoever believed in me without seeing me.' A man said to him: 'And what is Tuba?'" — the hadith continues.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Upon this interpretation which we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the transmission of it, it must be that the statement regarding the nominative case of God's words ﴿Good fortune is theirs﴾ is contrary to the view we related from the grammarians concerning it. This is because the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is that *Tuba* is the name of a tree in Paradise. Given that this is so, it is a proper noun, like Zayd and Amr. And when that is so, the words ﴿and a good place of return﴾ can only be in the nominative case, being conjoined to *Tuba*.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a good place of return﴾, He means: and a good place of return (*munqalab*) [[See the explanation of *al-ma'ab* earlier, 6:258, 259.]], as follows:

٢٠٣٩٦- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿and a good place of return﴾, that he said: "A good place of return."
[[See the explanation of *al-ma'ab* earlier, 6:258, 259.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 30:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Thus We have sent you (O Muhammad) among a community before which other communities have passed away, that you might recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him is my return.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: Thus We have sent you, O Muhammad, to a community of people [see the explanation of "ummah" in the previous lexical indices, under (ʾ-m-m)], meaning to a group, [while] before them there passed away groups upon the same likeness as that which they are upon, and they perished [see the explanation of "khala" previously, 350, footnote 3, and the references there]. ﴿That you might recite to them what We have revealed to you﴾, meaning: that you might convey to them what We sent you with, of My revelation which I revealed to you. ﴿While they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: while they deny the oneness of God and reject it. ﴿Say: He is my Lord﴾, meaning: if these people to whom I have sent you, O Muhammad, disbelieve in the Most Merciful, then you say: Allah is my Lord. ﴿There is no deity except Him. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him is my return﴾, meaning: to Him is my resort and my turning back.

* *

[This] is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I repented, a return (matab) and repentance (tawbah)" [see the explanation of "tawbah" previously in the lexical indices, under (t-w-b)].

* *

Scholars of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

20397. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ), at the time of Hudaybiyyah, when he made peace with Quraysh, wrote: "This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon." The idolaters of Quraysh said: "If you were the Messenger of God (ﷺ), we would not have fought you, we would have wronged you! But write: 'This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed upon.'" The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Let us, O Messenger of God, fight them!" He said: "No, but write as they wish, for I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah." When the scribe wrote "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," Quraysh said: "As for 'the Most Merciful,' we do not know it; the people of the Jahiliyyah used to write 'In Your name, O God.'" His companions said: "O Messenger of God, let us fight them!" He said: "No, but write as they wish."

20398. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Thus We have sent you among a community before which other communities have passed away﴾, to the end of the verse, he said: This is when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) corresponded with Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah, and he wrote: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." They said: "Do not write 'the Most Merciful,' for we do not know what 'the Most Merciful' is; write only 'In Your name, O God.'" God said: ﴿While they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him﴾, to the end of the verse.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be cleft asunder, or the dead could be made to speak! Nay, to Allah belongs the affair entirely.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation, exegesis) differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: ﴿and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾, and [the sentence] ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion﴾ means: they disbelieve in Allah even if the mountains were set in motion for them by this Qur'an. They said: this is from the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) which has the meaning of the anticipated (al-taqdim). They made the answer of "law" (if/had) precede it, because the speech is in the sense of their saying: "Even if this Qur'an were to set the mountains in motion or split the earth, they would still disbelieve in the Most Merciful."

Mention of those who said this:

2o399 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be cleft, or the dead could be made to speak﴾. He said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh. They said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you could widen the valleys of Makkah for us, and set its mountains in motion so that we could farm them, and bring our dead back to life, or split the earth for us, or make the dead speak!" So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be cleft, or the dead could be made to speak. Nay, to Allah belongs the affair entirely.﴾

2o400 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be cleft, or the dead could be made to speak﴾: [it is] the saying of the disbelievers of Quraysh to Muhammad: "Set our mountains in motion so that our land becomes spacious for us, for it is narrow; or bring Syria close to us, for we trade there; or bring our forefathers out of their graves, and we shall speak with them!" Then Allah the Exalted said [[The phrase "Then Allah the Exalted said" is missing from the manuscript, and it is necessary.]]: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be cleft, or the dead could be made to speak﴾.

2o401 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

2o402 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said: "They said: 'If the mountains were to be spread out for us, or the rivers were made to flow for us, or you spoke to the dead through it!' So this was revealed." Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: They said: "Set the mountains in motion by the Qur'an, split the earth by the Qur'an, bring our dead out by it."

2o403 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir said: They said: "If the mountains were spread out for us, or the rivers made to flow for us, or the dead spoken to through it!" Then it was revealed: ﴿Have not those who believe despaired?﴾

* * *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion﴾ is an independent, separate statement, cut off from His words: ﴿and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾. He said: The answer of "law" is omitted, the hearers' knowledge of the intended meaning having made its mention unnecessary. They said: The Arabs do this often, and among it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Had it been a soul that dies gently [[Its meaning: "suddenly and easily." From their saying "a light (sarih) matter," i.e. easy, or "a hasty matter," i.e. quick.]],
But it is a soul that is torn apart into pieces.

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Have not those who believe despaired that if Allah willed, He would guide all the people?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿Have not those who believe despaired﴾.

Some of the people of Basra claimed that its meaning is: "Did they not know and become clear?" and for his statement he cited the verse of Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi:

I say to them in the mountain pass when they capture me:
"Did you not despair? I am the son of the horseman Zahdam."

[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:332; Asas al-Balaghah (y-'-s); its takhrij by the scholar Sayyid Saqr in Mushkil al-Qur'an: 148; Gharib al-Qur'an: 228; al-Lisan (y-'-s). Its explanation is there, and in other places there are many. "Zahdam" was, they said, the horse of Suhaym. If the attribution of the poem to Suhaym is correct, then "Zahdam" was the horse of his father Wathil. This poem is attributed to Jabir ibn Suhaym, and if that is correct, then Zahdam was the horse of Suhaym. See Nasab al-Khayl of Ibn al-Kalbi: 17, and Asma' al-Khayl of Ibn al-A'rabi: 63.]]

It is narrated as "yaysirunani," and whoever narrated it as "yaysirunani" meant: they divide me up, from "maysir" (the game of chance), as a slaughtered camel is divided. And whoever narrated it as "ya'sirunani" meant captivity, and he said: By his saying "Did you not despair?" he meant: "Did you not know?" They also recited in this sense:

Did not the peoples despair that I am his son
Even though I am far from the land of my tribe?

[[Attributed to Malik ibn 'Awf, and to Riyah ibn 'Adi. Mu'jam Gharib al-Qur'an in the questions of Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, from Ibn 'Abbas: 291; al-Qurtubi: 9:320; Abu Hayyan: 5:392; Asas al-Balaghah (y-'-s). I do not know the poem.]]

They interpreted His words "Did he not despair" as: "Did he not know and become clear?"

* * *

It is mentioned from Ibn al-Kalbi that this is the dialect of a tribe of al-Nakha' called Wahbil; you say: "Did you not despair that such-and-such" in the sense of: "Did you not know it?"

* * *

It is mentioned from al-Qasim ibn Ma'n that it is the dialect of Hawazin, and that they say: "Yaisat such-and-such," meaning: I knew.

* * *

As for some of the Kufans, he denied this [[This is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, in explaining the verse, and what follows is the text of his words.]], and claimed that he had never heard any of the Arabs say "ya'isa" in the sense of "'alima" (to know). He himself says, regarding the meaning, although it is not heard: "ya'isa" in the sense of "'alima" (knew) is directed toward that, since it has been revealed to the believers that if Allah willed, He would guide all the people. So he said: "Have they not despaired knowingly?" meaning: knowledge makes them despair, so it is as if knowledge were implied in it, just as one says: "I have despaired of you that you will not succeed knowingly," as if it were said: "I knew it knowingly." He said: and the saying of the poet [[He is Labid.]]:

Until, when the archers despaired and released
Swift, well-trained hounds, dry-skinned, whose leashes [[Its meaning: they released upon it hounds with drooping ears, which are hunting dogs whose ears droop. "Dawajin" means ferocious ones that have been trained to hunt. "Al-qafil" means dry. "Al-a'sam" is the plural of "isam," which are leather collars placed on dogs' necks, and they are also called "sawajir."]]

Its meaning: until they despaired of everything possible, except what appeared to them, they released [the hounds]. So it is in the sense of: until they knew that there was no way except what they saw, and their knowledge ended, so whatever was beyond it became despair. [[In Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "fakana ma warahu yaasan" ("so what lay beyond it was despair"), which is good.]]

As for the people of ta'wil, they interpreted it in the sense of: "Did he not know and become clear?"

[[Report 2o410: "Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Taghlabi al-Ahwal," the teacher of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, is the companion of Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, known for his companionship with him, trustworthy and dependable.
