"Ya'la ibn Hakim" is reliable; the group narrated from him except al-Tirmidhi. He has passed under number 12748.

So this report's narrators are reliable; indeed all its narrators are narrators of the two Sahihs, except Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, who is an imam, trustworthy and truthful. Thus its chain is sound, with no flaw in it. Despite the soundness of its chain, I have not found any of the major compilers, such as Ahmad in his Musnad or al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, nor any of those who quoted from the major compilers, such as al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id, who related this report or mentioned this reading from Ibn 'Abbas or 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, as came in the report before it, number 2o408. Indeed, more surprising than that, Ibn Kathir, who critically examined Abu Ja'far's hadiths in the tafsir, when he reached the tafsir of this verse, did nothing except point to the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, and omitted this report in a way contrary to his usual practice. My strong opinion is that Ibn Kathir recognised the soundness of its chain, but he rejected the apparent meaning, which led him to remain silent about it; he ought to have mentioned it and described it as strange or objectionable, but he did not, because, in my view, he was perplexed about the soundness of its chain together with the objectionable sense indicated by its apparent wording. This apparent meaning became more objectionable to him because of what the earlier exegetes said about this report from Ibn 'Abbas, when they narrated it without a chain, with wordings other than these.

When I saw this from Ibn Kathir and others, I traced what the transmitters had related of the wording of the report, and I found between the wordings narrated without chains and the wording of Abu Ja'far with its chain a difference that is plainly evident. Their wordings are what led many of the imams to say a bad thing about this report, reaching the level of attacking its transmitter, calling him a heretic and an apostate! And indeed, what they said about the report they narrated in their wording is well founded. But as for this wording of Abu Ja'far, although its apparent sense is problematic, studying it in the proper way in which it ought to be studied removes from it the darkness of the corrupt meaning that comes to a person's mind at first reading.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 31 (part 2 of 2):

When I set about studying it from all its aspects, a great door of discussion opened up to me concerning this report and its like, such as the saying of ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers: "O nephew, the scribe made a mistake" (i.e., [a mistake] in what was written in the Imam Mushaf). God forbid that this should be the apparent meaning of the wording of her report. These two reports and others like them are taken up by the orientalists and their hangers-on, who attribute themselves to the people of Islam, as a pathway for attacking the Qur'an, or as a means of sowing confusion among those who have no knowledge of the revelation of the Mighty Qur'an. So the matter required me to write a comprehensive treatise explaining the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying: "The Qur'an was revealed in seven ahruf" (seven modes/dialects; ahruf, sing. harf, plural of harf, letter or mode of recitation), how these seven ahruf were, and what of them has remained with us. I concluded that, by God's praise, they all remain intact in the readings of the reciters (qira'at), in the anomalous readings (shadhdh), and in the transmission of the ahruf, not as Abu Ja'far al-Tabari held in the introduction to his tafsir (1: 55–59), nor as those who followed his view held. Then I explained what occurred regarding the writing of the Mushaf in the time of Abu Bakr, then the writing of the Imam Mushaf in the time of ʿUthman, may God be pleased with them both, and I made that an explanation that is sufficient and adequate, God willing. I had intended to make this treatise an introduction to the sixteenth part of Abu Ja'far's tafsir, but it grew long until it became a book, so I preferred to publish it separately as a book on its own, God willing.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said: that its interpretation is "have they not become clear and known," due to the consensus of the people of interpretation upon this, and the verses of poetry we have recited concerning it.

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: Even if there were a Qur'an other than this Qur'an by which mountains were set in motion, this Qur'an would set them in motion; or by which the earth was cut asunder, this would cut it asunder; or by which the dead were made to speak, this would make them speak. But that was not done with a Qur'an before this Qur'an so that it would be done with this one. [[The phrase in the printed edition was: "And if it were done with a Qur'an before this Qur'an, it would be done with this," which is utterly corrupt; its correct form is what is in the manuscript, and I do not know why it was changed.]] ﴿Rather, to God belongs the affair entirely﴾, meaning: all of it is to Him and in His hand. He guides whom He wills to faith, granting them success in it, and He leads astray whom He wills, forsaking them. Have not those who believe in God and His Messenger become clear—when they were eager for my response to those who asked their prophet for what they asked of him, namely the moving of the mountains away from them, [[The bracketed addition is required by the context; or the word "min" in "min taysir al-jibal" may be omitted from the speech.]] and the bringing near of the land of Syria to them, and the reviving of their dead—that if God willed, He would guide all people to faith in Him without the producing of a sign, or the bringing about of anything of what they asked to be brought about? God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: What then is the meaning of their desire for that, given their knowledge that guidance and destruction are to Me and in My hand, whether I send down a sign or do not send it? I guide whom I will without sending down a sign, and I lead astray whom I will even when a sign is sent down.

Commentary on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by a calamity, or it will descend near their home, until the promise of God comes. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise﴾ (13:31)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And will not cease﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ among your people, ﴿to be struck, for what they have done﴾ of their disbelief in God, their denial of you, and their expulsion of you from among them, ﴿by a calamity﴾, which is what strikes them of affliction, punishment and retribution: by killing at times, by wars at times, and by famine at times. ﴿Or it will descend﴾, you, O Muhammad, meaning: or you will alight, ﴿near their home﴾ with your army and companions, ﴿until the promise of God comes﴾, which He promised you concerning them, namely your victory over them, your conquest of their land, and your subduing them by the sword. ﴿Indeed, God does not fail in the promise﴾, meaning: God will fulfil for you, O Muhammad, what He promised you of victory over them, for He does not break His promise.

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿Messengers were certainly mocked before you, but I gave the disbelievers respite, then I seized them. So how was My punishment?﴾ [13:32]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "O Muhammad, if these polytheists of your people mock you and ask you for signs, denying what you have brought them, then be patient with their harm to you, persist in carrying out your Lord's command to warn them and to leave them without excuse,[[In the printed edition it reads "fi i'dharihim" (in their excuse-making), which is corrupt. The nun in "indharihim" in the manuscript was originally an ayn, which the copyist then made into a nun, so its written form became garbled. It is said: "a'dhartu ilayhi i'dhaaran," meaning I left him no place for excuse, because you have reached the utmost limit in conveying and clarifying the message.]] for nations before you have indeed mocked, and they passed on, and they mocked My messengers.[[In the printed edition it reads "birusul" without the yaa, which is a poor reading of the manuscript because the yaa is faint in the copyist's writing.]] I extended the respite for them, and I lengthened their term, then I brought down My punishment and My vengeance upon them when they persisted in their error and misguidance. So look at how My punishment was when I punished them. Did I not make them taste the painful torment, and make them a lesson for people of understanding?"

* *

In the speech of the Arabs, *al-imla'* (respite, from the root *amla*) means prolonging. It is said: "amlaytu li-fulan" when I prolonged the time for someone, and from it comes *al-mulawa min al-dahr* (a long period of time).[[See the explanation of *al-imla'* above, 7:421; and Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1:108, 333.]] And from it is the saying: "tamallaytu habiban,"[[In the printed edition it reads "tamallaytu hinan," which is a plain error.]] and for this reason night and day are called *al-malawan* because of their length, as Ibn Muqbil said:

Oh, the abodes of the tribe at al-Sab'an,
Worn away by the two *malawan* (long periods of night and day).[[The line, its sourcing, attribution and explanation were given earlier, 7:420, notes 3 and 4; and see Ibn Muqbil's poem in his Diwan, recently published: 335.]]

And the wide expanse of land is called *mala'*,[[See Majaz al-Qur'an 1:333.]] as the poet said:[[It is al-Tirmah, who was of the Tayy tribe.]]

So it drenched from it every worn-out and fresh (land),
And the swift camels carrying water-skins through the *mala' al-mutabatin* (the wide, spreading expanse).[[His Diwan, p. 168; al-Adhdad of al-Asma'i and Ibn al-Sikkit, pp. 44, 197; al-Adhdad of Ibn al-Anbari, p. 256; and Lisan (ayn). In the printed edition it reads "wajf al-rawaya," which also appears in some of the earlier sources and in the Diwan, but the manuscript has "wajeef." Although what follows is badly written and the poem of al-Tirmah as it appears in the Diwan is disordered, with much missing, some of it can be found in various places in Ibn Qutayba's al-Ma'ani al-Kabir, which indicates that lines were lost before this line. I could not determine the place of this line in his poem, so its meaning was obscure to me, because the pronoun in "minha" depends on a previous referent I could not locate. For the same reason I cannot determine which of the two readings, "wajf" or "wajeef," is more correct, though I lean toward the second. The vocabulary of the line: "akhdala" means became wet. "Siqa' 'ayn" is said when water flows from a water-skin, and "siqa' ayn" is a new usage in the dialect of Tayy, and al-Tirmah is of Tayy, so he is the one meant here. "Al-wajeef" is a kind of swift camel pace. "Al-rawaya" is the plural of "riwaya," the camel on which one draws water, carrying water-skins. "Al-mutabatin," in the commentary on his Diwan, means the lowered or flattened; likewise in Amali Abi 'Ali al-Qali 2:7, in the explanation of a woman's saying: "cast your eye over this *mala' mutabatin*." In my view this interpretation is not good in both places; it is from the expression "sha'w batin," meaning far and wide. al-Zamakhshari stated this in al-Asas, saying: "tabatana al-makan," meaning it stretched far apart. This is the correct sense of the word here, as we see.]]

For the length between its two ends and its extent.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned [as those who have no such power]? Yet they ascribe partners to God. Say: "Name them. Or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth, or of mere outward speech?" Rather, the scheming of those who disbelieve has been made attractive to them, and they have been barred from the way. And whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ (13:33).

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Is the Lord, who is ever-living and does not perish or cease, standing over the sustenance of all creatures, [[See the explanation of "al-qiyam" (standing/sustaining) above, 6:519-521 and 7:120-124. See also Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1:333.]] encompassing it, knowing them and the deeds they earn, watching over them, such that nothing is hidden from Him wherever they may be, [like one who is destroyed and perished, who neither hears nor sees nor understands anything, and who cannot repel from himself or from those who worship him any harm, nor bring to them any benefit?] Are the two equal?

* *

The answer has been omitted in this verse and not stated. It has been said that the sense is: "like so-and-so," leaving out what is meant, relying on the hearer's knowledge of what was mentioned in place of what was left unmentioned. This is because when He, glorified is His praise, said: ﴿and they ascribed partners to God﴾, it was known that the meaning of the speech is: "like their partners whom they took as gods." As the poet said: [[He is al-Qital al-Kilabi.]]

Choose, you have been chosen, O Umm 'Al... between a short one whose span is a tinbal... Is that one, or the one with the torn garment... and he never ceases at the end of nights...

Destroyer of wealth and acquirer of wealth. [[From a rajaz verse transmitted by the author of al-Aghani, 20:164, in a long narrative. Ihsan 'Abbas recorded it in his collection of al-Qital al-Kilabi's poetry: 83; the sourcing is at 113, and it is to be supplemented by Lisan (r-m-l), with variation in its transmission. "Umm 'Al" is "'Aliyya," a woman of the Banu Nasr ibn Mu'awiya, who was the wife of a man of the notables of the tribe, so al-Qital would mention her in his poetry. The version in al-Aghani is: "Choose, you have been chosen among the men," because before it is: "Perhaps we shall visit Umm 'Al."

In the printed edition it reads "qasir shadhu," which is an error.

It is said: "So-and-so is short of span" (qasir al-shibr) when he has a close stride; al-Zamakhshari said: close-set in build.

The version in al-Aghani reads "qasir ba'uhu." "Al-tinbal" means the short one. After this verse comes: "And his mother is a shepherdess of camels, spending the night between the fodder and the grain-heap."

"Munkhariq al-sirbal" means one whose sirbal (shirt) is torn. In al-Bakri's commentary on the verse of Layla al-Akhyaliyya: "One whose shirt is torn from him, you think him, in the midst of the tents, sick from shyness," there are two opinions: one, that this is an allusion to the needy pulling at him; the second, that he gives preference to others with his best garments and clothes them. The more correct view in my opinion is that they praise a man for being constantly on journeys and in raids, alternating between them, so that he is always in worn garments, because he is not settled and attached to the tribe, so he does not mind acquiring new garments; this belongs to the qualities of generosity and valor. After this verse, which confirms what I have said: "Generous paternal uncle and generous maternal uncle... destroyer of wealth and acquirer of wealth."

"And he never ceases at the end of nights, his she-camel stumbles in the naqal." "Mufid mal" means one who acquires wealth. The version in Lisan: "his she-camel trots in the naqal." "Tarmalu" means hastens. "Al-naqal" means the alternating gait, which is that she places her hind feet where her forelegs were, from her speed.]]

He did not say the answer, but he said "shubruhu tinbal," [[In the printed edition here also: "shiruhu."]] and between such and such, relying on his saying "Is that one, or the one with the torn garment," and the indication of the statement about the one with the torn garment is sufficient for his intended meaning in that.

Those who give interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil; ta'wil, interpretation/explanation of meaning) have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

2044o- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned﴾: That is your Lord, blessed and exalted, standing over the sons of Adam with their sustenance and their term of life, and guarding their deeds upon them, and God knows best. [[The report 2044o: in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:64, and the end of the report was dropped.]]

2044-1- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned﴾. He said: God stands over every soul. [[From the beginning of his saying, "He said...", is missing from the printed edition.]]

2044-2- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned﴾. He means by that Himself; He says: He is with you wherever you are, so no worker works except that God is present with him. It is said: They are the angels who were assigned to the sons of Adam. [[The report 2044-2: in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:64, and it limited itself to "He means by that Himself." In the printed edition it reads "except that He is present," differing from the manuscript. His saying "It is said: they are the angels..." is without doubt not from the saying of Ibn 'Abbas; it is probably from the saying of Muhammad ibn Sa'd, the narrator of the report.]]

2044-3- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned﴾, and over their provision and over their food; so I am standing over that, and they are my servants, [[In the manuscript: "So I am over that and they are my servants," dropping "standing."]] then they ascribed partners to me.

2044-4- It was reported from al-Husayn ibn Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned﴾: He is God, standing over every soul, pious and sinful, providing for them and protecting them, then among them whoever associates others with Him does so. [[The report 2044-4: in the printed edition, "ibn al-Faraj" is dropped from the chain, and he added to the text of the report, making it "over every soul, pious and sinful," whereas what I have established agrees with what is in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:64.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they ascribed partners to God. Say: Name them, or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth, or of mere outward speech?﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: I am the one who sustains these polytheists, and who directs their affairs, and who guards their deeds over them; and they have ascribed to me partners among my creation, whom they worship besides Me. Say to them, O Muhammad: Name these whom you have associated in the worship of God, for if they say "gods," they have lied, because there is no god but the One, the Subduer, with no partner — ﴿or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth﴾, meaning: Will you inform Him that there is a god on earth, when there is no god other than Him on earth or in the heavens?

* *

Those who give interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

2044-5- It was reported from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And they ascribed partners to God. Say: Name them﴾: Even if they named them gods, they would be lying and saying other than the truth, because God is One, having no partner. God said: ﴿Or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth, or of mere outward speech?﴾, meaning: God does not know any god other than Him on earth. [[The report 2044-5 is the completion of the earlier report in al-Durr al-Manthur 4:64.]]

2044-6- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they ascribed partners to God. Say: Name them﴾: and God created them.

2044-7- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And they ascribed partners to God. Say: Name them﴾: And even if they named them, they would lie and say what God does not know, "there is no god besides God." So that is His saying: ﴿Or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth﴾. [[In the printed edition, "ma" was dropped from "ma min ilah" ("there is no god") and that corrupted the sense.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or of mere outward speech﴾, it is heard, [[In the printed edition, "wa qawlihi" ("and His saying") was dropped, making the words one continuous context.]] and in reality it is falsehood with no validity.

* *

Those who give interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding that, except that they said: ﴿mere outward speech﴾ means: "mere falsehood," so they gave the meaning indicated by the word, without explaining the reality of its interpretation.

Those who said that:

2044-8- Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shababa narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Abu Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿mere outward speech﴾: by conjecture.

2044-9- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

2044-50- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿or of mere outward speech﴾: and "outward speech" is falsehood.

2044-51- It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿or of mere outward speech﴾, he says: or of falsehood and lies, even if they said false and lying words.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, the scheming of those who disbelieve has been made attractive to them﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There is no partner for God in the heavens or on earth, but the polytheists who call upon a god besides Him have had their scheming made attractive to them [[See the explanation of "al-tazyin" (making attractive) above, 15:55, note 3, and the references there.]], and that scheming is their fabrication and their lying against God. [[See the explanation of "al-makr" (scheming) above, p. 68, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Mujahid used to say: the meaning of "makr" here is "speech," as if he said: meaning their saying of associating others with God. [[In the printed edition "ya'ni" ("meaning") is dropped.]]

2044-52- Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, the scheming of those who disbelieve has been made attractive to them﴾, he said: their saying.

2044-53- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they have been barred from the way﴾, the reciters differed regarding its recitation.

The common reciters of Kufa recited it: ﴿wa suddu 'an al-sabil﴾ with the "sad" vowelled with a damma, meaning: God barred them from His way because of their disbelief in Him; then the "sad" was made with a damma because the doer was not named (passive voice).

* *

As for the common reciters of the Hijaz and Basra, they recited it with a fatha on the "sad," meaning that the polytheists are the ones who barred people from the way of God. [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" (barring) above, 15:285, note 1, and the references there.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that it should be said: these are two well-known readings, each recited by leading reciters, and their meanings are close, because the polytheists were barred from belief in God, and at the same time they worshipped others, as God described them in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to bar [people] from the way of God﴾ [al-Anfal: 36].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whomever God leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whomever God leaves astray from reaching the truth and guidance, by forsaking him, for him there is no one who can guide him to reaching them, because that is not attained except by God's success and help, and that is in God's hand and toward Him, not in the hand of anyone else besides Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 34:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿For them is a punishment in the life of this world, but the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and they will have no protector from Allah﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, exalted is He, says: For these disbelievers whose description He has given in this surah, there is a punishment in the life of this world by killing, captivity, and the calamities which Allah afflicts them with. ﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe﴾, meaning: Allah's punishment of them in the Hereafter is more intense than His punishment of them in this world.

"Ashaqq" (more severe) is an "af'al" form derived from "al-mashaqqah" (hardship).

* *

As for His words, ﴿and they will have no protector from Allah﴾, His mention, exalted is He, says: These disbelievers will have no one who protects them from the punishment of Allah when He punishes them, neither a close friend (hamim), nor a guardian (wali), nor a helper (nasir), because He, majestic is His majesty, has no equal (la yu'addu) who could oppose Him and overpower Him, [["'adda, ya'uddu, 'idadan wa mu'adah" means he opposed and rivaled him; "al-'idd" with a kasra on the 'ain means equal, with a kasra followed by a sukun.]] so as to rescue them from His punishment by force [[In the printed edition: "fayakhallisahu" and "takhallasahu" means rescued (istanqadha).]], and no one intercedes with Him except by His permission, and He does not permit anyone to intercede for one who disbelieved in Him and died in his disbelief without repenting from it.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 13, verse 35:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow; its food is everlasting, and so is its shade. That is the final outcome of those who were righteous, and the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning what the subject (murafa') of "al-mathal" (the likeness) is.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: The element that raises "al-mathal" is His saying, ﴿beneath it rivers flow﴾, in meaning. He said: It is as when you say: "The description (hilyah) of so-and-so: a dark-complexioned man of such-and-such," so "al-asmar" (the dark-complexioned one) is not raised by "al-hilyah"; rather it is a beginning (ibtida'), meaning: he is dark-complexioned, he is such-and-such. He said: If "anna" (that) were inserted in such a case, it would be correct. He said: A similar usage in speech is: "Your likeness is that you are such-and-such and that you are such-and-such." And His saying: ﴿Then let man look at his food, that We [anna] poured down water﴾ [Surah Abasa: 24–25]. Whoever reads it this way, [reads] ﴿the likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised, therein...﴾. And whoever reads "anna ṣababnā al-mā'" (that We poured the water) makes the noun apparent, because it is governed by reference back to "al-ta'am" (food) in the genitive, and it is a resumption (mustani'), meaning: his food is that We poured down water, then We did such-and-such. He said: The meaning of His saying ﴿the likeness of the Garden﴾ is the attributes of the Garden.

* *

Some of the Basran grammarians said: The meaning of that is: the description of the Garden. He said: From it is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest likeness﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 27], meaning: to God belongs the highest attribute. He said: So the meaning of the statement in His saying ﴿the likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised, beneath it rivers flow﴾, or "therein are rivers," is as if He said: the description of the Garden is a description, beneath it rivers flow, or a description wherein are rivers, and God knows best.

He said: Another aspect: it is as if, when it is said ﴿the likeness of the Garden﴾, it is then said: the Garden which the righteous have been promised. He said: Likewise is His saying ﴿Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 30], as if He said: by God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and God knows best.

He said: And His saying ﴿for what I neglected concerning the side of God﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 56] means: concerning the essence of God; it is as if, in our view, it was said: concerning God.

He said: Likewise His saying ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 11]: the meaning is only: there is nothing like a thing, and there is nothing like Him, because He has no likeness. He said: This is not like your saying to a man: "There is no one like you," because it is possible for him to have a likeness, whereas God, that is not permissible for Him. He said: Similar to it is the verse of Labid:

"Until the year is complete, then peace be upon you both"

He said: It has been explained to us that he meant: "peace be upon you both." Aws ibn Hajar said:

"And slain nobles like the logs, overwhelmed by a pouring torrent of rain"

He said: The meaning in our view is "like the logs," because he did not intend to make a likeness for the logs and then liken the slain to it. He said: Similar to it is the verse of Umayya:

"Saturn and the Bull beneath the foot of his right hand, and the Eagle for the other, and a watchful Lion"

He said: He said "beneath the foot of his right hand," as if he said: beneath his foot, or beneath his right foot. He said: And the verse of Labid:

"He lost his herd, and a rain-cloud as a guest came upon him, its command in the hand of the north wind"

It is as if he said: its command was with the north wind, and toward the north wind. And also Labid's verse:

"Until, when it cast a hand into the darkness..."

It is as if he said: until it fell into the darkness.

* *

Another of them said: It is of the withholding of its predicate (al-makfūf 'an khabarihi). This is the view of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an. He said: The Arabs do this. He said: It has another meaning: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]﴾ [13:18] is the likeness of the Garden, connected, a description of it according to the first statement. This is also the view of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an. His saying "for those who responded" is verse 18 of Surah al-Ra'd, and this verse is 35 of it, so he said "according to the first statement."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these statements is that it is said: the likeness was mentioned, saying ﴿the likeness of the Garden﴾, and what is meant is the Garden; then the Garden was described by its attributes, because its likeness is only its description, and its description is not something other than it. Since that is so, and then "the likeness" was mentioned, saying ﴿the likeness of the Garden﴾, and its likeness is its description and the description of the Garden, its description was like the description of "the likeness," and it is as if the speech proceeded by mentioning the Garden, so it was said: the Garden, beneath it rivers flow, as the poet said:

"I see the passing of years has taken from me what the crescent's waning takes from the new moon"

He mentioned "the passing" (al-marr), and in the report returned to "the years."

And His saying ﴿its food is everlasting, and so is its shade﴾ means: what is eaten therein; He says: it is everlasting for its people, not cut off from them, and it does not cease or perish, but it is permanent without end. ﴿And so is its shade﴾ means: its shade is also everlasting, because there is no sun in it.

* *

﴿That is the final outcome of those who were righteous﴾ means: this is the Garden whose attributes He, mighty is His praise, described, the outcome of those who feared God, avoiding His disobedience and performing His obligations.

And His saying ﴿and the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire﴾ means: the final outcome of those who disbelieve in God is the Fire.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 36:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been sent down to you, and among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say: I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.﴾ (13:36)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those to whom We sent down the Book from among those who believed in you and followed you, O Muhammad, ﴿rejoice at what has been sent down to you﴾ from Him. ﴿And among the factions (al-ahzab) are those who deny part of it﴾ — meaning: among the people of the religions who band together against you, and they are people of various creeds [see the explanation of "al-ahzab" above, 15:278, note 1, and the references there] — those who deny some of what has been sent down to you. So say to them: ﴿I have only been commanded﴾, O people, ﴿to worship Allah﴾ alone, apart from whatever else is worshipped, ﴿and not to associate anything with Him﴾, so that I make a partner for Him in my worship and worship the gods and idols alongside Him; rather, I single out the religion for Him, as a upright monotheist (hanif) and a Muslim. ﴿To Him I invite﴾, meaning: to His obedience and to sincere worship of Him I invite people. ﴿And to Him is my return﴾, meaning: to Him is my final destination.

* *

"Ma'ab" is a form of "maf'al" from the saying of the speaker: "aba yaubu, awban wa ma'aban" (he returned, a return and a returning).

[See the explanation of "al-ma'ab" above, 4:444, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

20454- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been sent down to you﴾: they are the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, who rejoiced in the Book of Allah and His Messenger and affirmed it.

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾, he meant the Jews and the Christians.

20455- al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾, he said: from the People of the Book.

20456- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

20457- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been sent down to you, and among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾, [he said:] from the People of the Book, and "al-ahzab" are the People of the Books, whom their factionalism brings close together. [In the printed edition: "their dispersal for their war," but what I have affirmed is what is in the manuscript, though the first word was written rather badly.] Regarding His saying: ﴿If the factions (al-ahzab) come﴾ [33:20], he said: because of their banding together against the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Jurayj said, and he said, from Mujahid: ﴿deny part of it﴾, he said: part of the Qur'an.

20458- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding: ﴿And to Him is the return﴾: to Him is the destination of every servant.

20459- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been sent down to you﴾: this refers to those among the People of the Book who believed in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they rejoice in that. And he recited: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it﴾ [10:40]. And regarding His saying: ﴿And among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾, he said: "al-ahzab" are the nations: the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians; among them are those who believed in it and among them are those who denied it.

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. And if you were to follow their desires after knowledge has come to you, you would have no protector or defender against God.﴾ (13:37)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as We sent down the Book to you, O Muhammad, and some of the factions (al-ahzab) denied it, so too We sent down the judgment and the religion as an Arabic judgment [[See the explanation of "al-hukm" (judgment) above in this volume: 23, note 1, and the references there.]]. He made it "Arabic" and described it as such because it was sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, who was an Arab. He attributed the religion to him because it was sent down upon him, yet the factions denied it. Then He, may His praise be exalted, forbade him from abandoning what was sent down to him and from following the factions, and He threatened him for doing so, saying: ﴿And if you follow﴾ their ﴿desires﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the desires of these factions, their pleasure and their love [[See the explanation of "al-hawa" (desire) above: 9: 302 / 11: 397.]], and you turn from your religion to their religion, you would have no one to shield you from the punishment of God if He punished you for following their desires, and no helper to support you and rescue you from God if He were to punish you.﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-wali" (protector) above: 13: 152, note 1, and the references there.]] He means: beware of following their desires.

* *

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and gave them wives and offspring. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of God. For every term there is a Book.﴾ (13:38)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And We had certainly sent﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿messengers before you﴾ to nations that passed away before your community. We made them human beings like you, with wives whom they married and offspring whom they produced [[See the explanation of "al-dhurriyyah" (offspring) above: 423, note 3, and the references there.]]. We did not make them angels who neither eat, nor drink, nor marry; so that We would make the messenger to your people one of the angels like them. Rather, We sent to them human beings like them, just as We sent to those before them, among all the other nations, human beings like them. ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of God.﴾ God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: No messenger whom God sends to His creation has the power to bring his community a sign or proof, ﴿such as moving mountains, transporting a city from one place to another, bringing the dead to life, and other such signs [[See the explanation of "al-ayah" (sign) above in the lexical indices: (ayy).]]﴾, ﴿except by the permission of God﴾, meaning: except by God's command to the mountains to move, to the earth to shift, and to the dead to come to life. ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾ means: for every term that God has decreed, there is a decree which He has written, and it is with Him. [[See the explanation of "al-ajal" (term) above: 15: 100, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-kitab" (book) above: 14: 90, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been said that its meaning is: for every Book that God has sent down from heaven there is a term.

Those who said this:

20460. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding God's words ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾: "It means: for every book that is sent down from heaven there is a term, and God erases what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book." [[The narration 20460: "al-Muthanna" is "al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim al-Amuli," a teacher of al-Tabari who has appeared many times before. "Ishaq ibn Yusuf" is perhaps "Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Wasiti," who appeared under numbers 3339, 4224, and 12742.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This, according to this view, is similar to God's saying: ﴿And the agony of death has come with truth﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:19]. Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, used to read it: ﴿And the agony of truth has come with death﴾. That is because the agony of death comes with the truth, and the truth comes with it. Likewise, the term has a book, and the book has a term.
