Those who said this:

20460. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding God's words ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾: "It means: for every book that is sent down from heaven there is a term, and God erases what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book." [[The narration 20460: "al-Muthanna" is "al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim al-Amuli," a teacher of al-Tabari who has appeared many times before. "Ishaq ibn Yusuf" is perhaps "Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Wasiti," who appeared under numbers 3339, 4224, and 12742.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This, according to this view, is similar to God's saying: ﴿And the agony of death has come with truth﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:19]. Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, used to read it: ﴿And the agony of truth has come with death﴾. That is because the agony of death comes with the truth, and the truth comes with it. Likewise, the term has a book, and the book has a term.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [13:39].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Allah effaces what He wills of the affairs of His servants and changes it, except for misery and happiness, for these two are not changed.

Those who said this:

20461 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Bahr ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: Allah manages the affairs of the servants, so He effaces what He wills, except misery, happiness, [life] and death.

[Note on the narration: Abu Kurayb is Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' ibn Kurayb al-Kufi, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), the teacher of al-Tabari, who has appeared countless times. As for Bahr ibn Isa, this is something I did not recognize, and I found no mention of him in any book despite lengthy searching; however, I strongly favour that the correct form of this chain is: "Abu Kurayb said: Bakr narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal..." And the explanation of that: Ibn Abi Layla is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari, who has appeared many times; 'Isa is 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari, who narrated from his great-uncle Ibn Abi Layla Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman; Ibn Sa'd said: "He heard the Musannaf of Ibn Abi Layla"; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib and elsewhere. And Bakr is Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari, also called Bakr ibn 'Ubayd, who narrated from his cousin 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar; and Abu Kurayb narrated from this Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Because of this correct context of the narration, I have concluded that the correct reading is "Bakr narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Layla," and perhaps that is from his Musannaf which 'Isa ibn al-Mukhtar narrated from him, and Allah knows best.

This report was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4:65), attributing it to 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab in full; the phrase between the brackets is from it, and from Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4:536). He mentioned the report from al-Thawri, Waki', and Hushaym, from Ibn Abi Layla, as will come in the following reports from 20463 to 20466.]

20462 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ... Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: Everything other than happiness and misery, for these two have already been decided.

[Note on the narration: Ibn Bashshar is Muhammad ibn Bashshar al-'Abdi, Bundar, Abu Bakr the memorizer, the teacher of Abu Ja'far, who has appeared countless times. Ibn Abi Layla is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who has preceded in the previous report. I have placed dots between the two men because this chain is invalid and cannot stand, since Ibn Abi Layla died in 148 AH and Ibn Bashshar was born in 167 AH and died in 252 AH; this is decisive evidence that something has dropped from the chain. My opinion is that its correct form is: "Ibn Bashshar said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Layla," because the two reports after it are through Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Layla, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrates from Waki', and Waki' narrates from Sufyan, and Allah knows best.]

20463 - 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us; and Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us; from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, saying regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾: he said: Except misery and happiness, and death and life.

20464 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn and Qabisa narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same.

20465 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Except life and death, and misery and happiness.

20466 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Book﴾, he said: Allah decrees the matter of the year on the Night of Power, except misery, happiness, death and life.

20467 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, he said: Except life and death, and happiness and misery, for these two do not change.

20468 - 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn 'Uqba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

[Note on the narration: Mu'adh ibn 'Uqba — I found no mention of him, and I have been unable to determine who he is, or what confusion entered this chain. I fear it may be: "Mu'adh ibn Hisham al-Dastawa'i" from "'Uqba," a corruption of something else such as "Shu'ba."]

20469 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

20470 - ... He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: I said to Mujahid: "If You have written me as happy, then confirm me; and if You have written me as miserable, then efface me." He said: Misery and happiness have already been decided.

[Note on the narration: "If You have written me as happy..." refers to the supplication of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, as will come in the following reports until the end of the explanation of the verse. The dots here indicate that the narration is from Ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari, as in the one before it.]

20471 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid — he said: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, he said: Allah sends down everything in the year on the Night of Power, so He effaces what He wills of the terms, the provisions and the decrees, except misery and happiness, for these two are firm.

[Note on the narration: Ahmad is Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Isa al-Ahwazi, the teacher of Abu Ja'far, who has preceded many times; see nos. 159 and 1841. Abu Ahmad is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Zubayri, who has also preceded; see nos. 159 and 1841. Then see the earlier chains no. 20463 and 20470. The second chain in this report: Sa'id ibn Sulayman al-Dabbi, Sa'dawayh, who has appeared many times, the last being no. 18511; the one who narrates from him is Ahmad ibn Ishaq, the teacher of al-Tabari. In the printed edition it was "ibn Sulayman," which is an error.]

20472 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: I asked Mujahid, saying: "What do you think of the supplication of one of us who says: 'O Allah, if my name is among the happy, then confirm it among them, and if it is among the wretched, then efface it and place it among the happy'?" He said: It is good. Then I came to him after a year or more, and asked him about that, and he said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night; indeed, We were warning. In it every wise matter is distinguished﴾ [44:3-4]. He said: In the Night of Power is decreed what will occur in the year of provision or calamity, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the book of misery and happiness, it is firm and does not change.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is that Allah effaces what He wills and establishes from a book other than the Mother of the Book, which is not changed in any part.

Those who said this:

20473 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: There are two books: a book from which He effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.

20474 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: The Book is two books: a book from which Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.

20475 - ... He said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same.

20475m - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ikrima, who said: The Book is two books: "Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book."

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that He effaces everything He wills, and establishes everything He intends.

Those who said this:

20476 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthham narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, that he used to say: "O Allah, if You have written us as miserable, then efface us and write us as happy; and if You have written us as happy, then confirm us, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book."

20477 - 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, who said: He used to frequently supplicate with these words: "O Allah, if You have written us as miserable, then efface us and write us as happy; and if You have written us as happy, then confirm us, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book."

[Note on the two narrations: Shaqiq is Shaqiq ibn Salama al-Asadi al-Kufi, who is Abu Wa'il, as in the second chain, who has appeared very many times. He was the most knowledgeable of the people of Kufa concerning the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, so his saying "he used to frequently supplicate" — the pronoun in it refers to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4:536) in a manner that gives the impression that it is Shaqiq ibn Salama himself who used to frequently supplicate, and he erred, for he is the one who changed the wording of the second report. See also al-Durr al-Manthur (4:67).]

20478 - ... He said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal... Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Hakima, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said while circumambulating the House and weeping: "O Allah, if You have written against me a misery or a sin, then efface it, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book; so make it happiness and forgiveness."

[Note on the narration: Mu'adh ibn Hisham is al-Dastawa'i, from whom the whole group narrated, who has appeared many times, among them nos. 4523, 5552, 6321. His father is Hisham ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, Sanbar, Abu Bakr al-Rab'i, of Bakr ibn Wa'il, a trustworthy narrator biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (4/2/198), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/59). Abu Hakima — his name is 'Isma, and it is said al-Ghazzal; he narrated from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, and from him narrated Qurra and Salam ibn Miskin, al-Dahhak ibn Yasar, and Hammad ibn Salama, and Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi. Abu Hatim said: "His rank is truthfulness." Ahmad mentioned him in Kitab al-'Ilal (1:18) and said: "Abu Hakima, 'Isma, narrated from him Qurra, and I think al-Taymi narrates from him." See the commentary on the following report; he is biographed in al-Kabir (4/1/63), al-Saghir (140), and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/30). Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mill; he lived in the Jahiliyya and embraced Islam in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) but did not meet him, and he has appeared many times, the last being no. 17151. Ibn Kathir transmitted it with this chain in his tafsir (4:536), adding in the chain: "from Abu Hakima 'Isma." Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4:66), attributing it to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir. See the commentary on the following reports.]

20479 - ... al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hakima, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: And I think I heard it from Abu 'Uthman, the same.

[Note on the narration: Mu'tamir is Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated, who has appeared many times. His father is Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, Abu al-Mu'tamir, trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated, who has appeared many times, including no. 6820. This chain confirms the surmise of Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him, when he said: "I think al-Taymi narrates from him," as preceded in the explanation of the earlier chain.]

20480 - ... He said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Isma Abu Hakima, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from 'Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, the same.

[Note on the narration: Qurra ibn Khalid al-Sadusi, trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated, who has appeared many times; see no. 9762. In the printed edition it was "'Isma ibn Abi Hakima," differing from the manuscript, and the manuscript had "'Isma ibn Hakima"; both are errors, as indicated by what we have set out in the note on report 20478. From the route of "Qurra, from 'Isma," al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Kabir (4/1/63), "from 'Abd Allah, Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us," and its wording: "O Allah, if You have written against me a sin, or a sinful deed, or rancour, then forgive it for me, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book." Al-Dulabi narrated it in al-Kuna wa al-Asma' (1:155), saying: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, from Qurra, and he did not say "or rancour," and he said: "Forgive me, and efface it from me, for You..."]

20481 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Hakima narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi say: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, while circumambulating the Ka'ba: "O Allah, if You have written me among the people of happiness, then confirm me therein; and if You have written against me sin and misery, then efface me and confirm me among the people of happiness, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book."

[Note on the narration: al-Muthanna is al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim al-Amuli, the teacher of al-Tabari, who has preceded many times. al-Hajjaj is al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal al-Anmati, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, whom the whole group narrated from, who has appeared many times; see no. 682. Hammad is Hammad ibn Salama ibn Dinar, who has appeared many times; see 20342.]

20482 - ... He said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilaba, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he used to say: "O Allah, if You have written me among [the people of] misery, then efface me and confirm me among the people of happiness."

[Note on the narration: The words between the brackets are an addition in the printed edition; the manuscript has "among the miserable." See the note on the next report, no. 20484.]

20483 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he says: It is the man who acts for a time in obedience to Allah, then returns to disobedience to Allah, and dies in his error — this is the one who is effaced; and the one who is established: the man who acts in disobedience to Allah, while good has already preceded for him, until he dies while in obedience to Allah — this is the one who is established.

[Note on the narration: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4:65), and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim. In the manuscript, in place of "and dies in his error," it reads "and returns in his error."]

20484 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Humayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ukaym, from 'Abd Allah, that he used to say: "O Allah, if You have written me among the happy, then confirm me among the happy, for You efface what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book."

[Note on the narration: Hilal ibn Humayd, also said Hilal ibn Abi Humayd, or Ibn 'Abd Allah, or Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, or Ibn Miqlas, al-Juhani, also called Hilal al-Wazzan. al-Bukhari said: "Waki' said once: Hilal ibn Humayd, and once: Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah, and it is not authentic." See al-'Ilal of Ahmad (1:106, 211). Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Hilal ibn Abi Humayd al-Wazzan, Abu Jahm al-Sayrafi; it is said Abu Umayya; he is Hilal ibn Miqlas al-Jahbadh, client of Juhayna," and Ibn Sa'd said similarly. Hilal is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/207), Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/75), and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (6:227). 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ukaym al-Juhani, Abu Ma'bad, was old, lived in the Jahiliyya and reached the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), but no authentic hearing from him is known; biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (3/1/39), Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/121), and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (6:77).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 39 (part 2 of 3):

It appears in the printed edition as "Abd Allah ibn Hakim," and in Ibn Kathir's tafsir (4: 536) as "Abd Allah ibn Alim." Both are errors.

This report was cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4: 536), and al-Suyuti took it up in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 67), attributing it additionally to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani. He transmitted it in a single form identical to the earlier report (no. 20482), with a difference in wording.

20485. al-Muthanna told me: al-Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us, from Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim, that Ka'b said to Umar, may Allah have mercy on him: "O Commander of the Faithful, were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would inform you of what will occur until the Day of Resurrection." He said: "And what is it?" He said: the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.﴾

[[Report 20485: "al-Hajjaj" is al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, who preceded shortly before, under no. 20481.
"Hammad" is Hammad ibn Salama, who has appeared many times. In Ibn Kathir's tafsir (4: 537) this report is related with "Khassaf" in place of Hammad, but I judge it to be "Hammad," as in the manuscript as well.
"Khassaf" is Khassaf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jazari, who is not reliable (laysa bi-dhak), biographed in Lisan al-Mizan (2: 397) and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/404).
"Abu Hamza" is Maymun al-A'war al-Tammar al-Ra'i al-Kufi, the companion of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. He is very weak, and his narrations have been abandoned. al-Uqayli said: "His narrations from Ibrahim in particular are not followed by others." He has appeared earlier under nos. 6190 and 11810. See al-Kuna of al-Dulabi (1: 157).
"Ibrahim" is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i, who has appeared many times.
This chain is extremely weak. It is strange that Sayyid Rashid Rida, in his commentary on Ibn Kathir (4: 537), says: "It is strange that boldness toward Ka'b should reach this degree of falsehood, both in law and in reason, and then his religion and knowledge are relied upon and reported from him. The strange thing is his prejudice against Ka'b al-Ahbar before verifying the chain of the report. What is Ka'b's fault if Abu Hamza al-A'war afflicted him with that?" But this is the sheikh's habit: whenever Ka'b al-Ahbar is mentioned, he accuses him without evidence.
al-Suyuti cited this report in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 67) and attributed it to no one other than Ibn Jarir.]]

20486. I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾, the verse: "He says: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾," meaning: I abrogate what I wish, and I do of the actions what I wish. If I wish, I add to them, and if I wish, I reduce them.

20487. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us: Affan told us: Hammam told us: al-Kalbi told us, concerning: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, that He: "effaces (yamha) from the provision and increases it, and effaces from the term and increases it."

[[Report 20487: This is how it appears in the manuscript, "yumha" as well, which is correct: "mahā al-shay' yamhūhu, wa-yamhāhu, mahwan wa-mahyan." What is in the other references is "yamhū."
See what will follow: 492, note 1.]]

I said: "From whom did you narrate this to me?" He said: "Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah ibn Ri'ab al-Ansari, from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Then al-Kalbi came later, and was asked about this verse: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, and he said: "He writes down the whole saying. Then, when Thursday comes, everything in it that carries no reward and no punishment is cast out, such as your saying: 'I ate, I drank, I entered, I went out,' and that sort of speech; and it is true. He establishes what has reward in it and punishment upon it."

[[Report 20487: "al-Kalbi" is Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, the genealogist and exegete, about whom there is speech to the extent that his narration cannot be relied upon. al-Tabari's own statement about him has preceded: "He is not among those whose transmission can be used as evidence" (1: 66). This is among the few places in the tafsir of Abu Ja'far where a report from al-Kalbi appears. See what preceded: 72, 246, 248, 12967.
This report was transmitted by Ibn Sa'd in Tabaqat al-Kabir, abridged (3/2/114). al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 66), attributing it additionally to Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 537). See the following chain. In the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir it reads: "and the like of that speech."]]

20488. al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Wahhab told us: I heard al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, similarly, and it did not go beyond Abu Salih.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Allah abrogates (yansakh) whatever of the rulings of His Book He wills, and establishes whatever of them He wills, so He does not abrogate it.

Those who said this:

20489. al-Muthanna told me, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, who said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾, he said: "From the Qur'an. He means: Allah replaces what He wills and abrogates it, and establishes what He wills and does not replace it." ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he means: "The whole of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book: the abrogating and the abrogated, what is replaced and what is established. All of that is in a Book."

[[Report 20489: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 67), attributing it additionally to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Madkhal. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 538).]]

20490. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, concerning his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, that it is like His saying: "Whatever verse We abrogate or cause you to forget, We bring one better than it or the like of it" (Surat al-Baqara: 106). And His saying: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾: that is, the whole of the Book and its origin.

20491. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, what He wills, and He is the Wise. ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, and its origin.

20492. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾: "by what is sent down to the prophets. ﴿And establishes﴾ what He wills of what is sent down to the prophets." He said: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, which is not changed or replaced.

20493. al-Qasim told us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾, he said: "He abrogates." He said: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: "the Reminder (al-dhikr)."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: He effaces the one whose term has come, and establishes the one whose term has not yet come, until his term.

Those who said this:

20494. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan concerning his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾: he says: "He effaces the one whose term has come and passed, and the one established, who is living, runs on to his term."

20495. Amr ibn Ali told us: Yahya told us: Awf told us: I heard al-Hasan say: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾, he said: "the one whose term has come," ﴿and establishes﴾, he said: "the one whose term has not yet come, until his term."

20496. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us: Hawdha told us: Awf told us, from al-Hasan, the like of the report of Ibn Bashshar.

20497. ... He said: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata told us: Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, concerning his saying: ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾, he said: "The terms of the children of Adam are in a Book. ﴿Allah effaces what He wills﴾ of their term ﴿and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾."

20498. ... He said: Shababa told us: Warqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾. When it was revealed: ﴿It is not for any messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's permission﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd: 38), the Quraysh said: "We do not see you, O Muhammad, possessing anything, and the matter has been finished!" So this verse was revealed as a threat and warning to them: "Indeed, if We wish, We bring about a new matter of Ours as We wish, and We renew it every Ramadan, and We efface and establish whatever We will of the provisions of the people and their afflictions, what We give them, and what We allot to them."

[[Report 20498: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 5), attributing it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 538).]]

20499. al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abd Allah told us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

20500. al-Qasim told us, who said: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: and He forgives whatever of the sins of His servants He wills, and leaves whatever He wills without forgiveness.

* *

Those who said this:

20501. Ibn Humayd told us: Hakkam told us, from Amr, from Ata, from Sa'id, concerning his saying: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and establishes﴾, he said: "He establishes in the womb wretchedness and happiness and everything. So He forgives of it what He wills and delays what He wills."

[[Report 20501: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 68) and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir. His wording there is: "... and everything that is existing, so He advances of it what He wills ...," and this is better than what is in our manuscript.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings mentioned concerning the interpretation of this verse, and the most similar to the truth, is the saying we have related from al-Hasan and Mujahid. That is because Allah, may He be remembered, threatened the polytheists who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for signs with punishment, and warned them with it, and said to them: ﴿It is not for any messenger to bring a sign except by Allah's permission. For every term there is a Book﴾. He informs them by this that there is for His judgment concerning them a fixed term written in a Book, and they are delayed until the time when that term comes. Then He said to them: When that term comes, Allah brings about what He wills of one whose term has drawn near and whose provision has been cut off, or whose destruction has arrived, or whose humiliation after exaltation, or the ruin of his wealth. He decrees that among His creation, and that is His effacing. And He establishes whatever He wills of one whose term, provision and enjoyment remain, [[al-Ukl, with a vowel on the alif and sukun on the kaf, is one's share of this world: of remaining and provision.]] so He leaves him as he is, and does not efface him.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has come with this meaning, and it is this:

20502. Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Asker told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd told us, from Ziyada ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah opens the Reminder in the three hours that remain of the night. In the first of those hours He looks into the Book which no one but Him looks into, so He effaces what He wills and establishes." Then he mentioned what is in the last two hours.

[[Report 20502: "Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Asker" is the sheikh of al-Tabari, who has appeared many times. See 5598, 5664, 5911.
"Ibn Abi Maryam" is Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, who is Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, a trustworthy transmitter from whom the whole group related. He has appeared many times, the last under no. 18404.
"Ziyada ibn Muhammad al-Ansari" is one whose narrations are rejected (munkar al-hadith), who has appeared under nos. 16943 and 16944.
This report has preceded at length under no. 16943, and its takhrij and the explanation of its chain were given there. It is the report to which al-Bukhari alluded in al-Kabir, saying: "munkar al-hadith." Additionally cited in its takhrij: al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 65), attributing it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 537). See the following report and the comment on it.]]

20503. Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli told me: Adam told us, who said: al-Layth told us: Ziyada ibn Muhammad told us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah descends in the three hours that remain of the night. In the first hour He opens the Reminder, which no one but Him has seen, and He effaces what He wills and establishes what He wills."

[[Report 20503: "Musa ibn Sahl ibn Qadim al-Ramli" is the sheikh of al-Tabari, a trustworthy transmitter. He has appeared under nos. 878, 5434, and 16944. See also "Musa ibn Sahl al-Razi," no. 180 and the comment on it, and "Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi," nos. 180, 4319, and 9482, and the comments on them.
"Adam" is Adam ibn Abi Iyas.
This is another route for the report that preceded, and so it is rejected (munkar) like its like.]]

20504. Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Asker told me: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Indeed Allah has a preserved tablet, the distance of five hundred years, of white pearl, which has two covers of ruby, and the two covers are two tablets for Allah. Each day He looks at it three hundred and sixty glances, He effaces what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book."

[[Report 20504: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 65) and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 537).]]

20505. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from his father, who said: A man told me, from his father, from Qays ibn Abbad, that he said: "The tenth of Rajab is the day on which Allah effaces what He wills."

[[Report 20505: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 66) and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir. He then mentioned after it a lengthy report from Qays ibn Abbad, and attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ (39)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And with Him is the lawful and the unlawful."

Those who said this:

20506. al-Muthanna told me: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us: Muhammad ibn Uqba told us: Malik ibn Dinar told us, who said: I asked al-Hasan. I said: "﴿The Mother of the Book﴾?" He said: "The lawful and the unlawful." I said to him: "Then what is ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾?" He said: "This is the Mother of the Qur'an."

* *

Others said: its meaning is: "And with Him is the whole of the Book and its origin."

Those who said this:

20507. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, concerning his saying: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: "The whole of the Book and its origin."

20508. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

20509. I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning his saying: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: "A Book with the Lord of the worlds."

20510. al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq ibn Yusuf told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: "The whole of the Book and its knowledge," meaning by that what is abrogated of it and what is established.

20511. al-Muthanna told me: Abu Salih told us: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he says: "And the whole of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book: the abrogating and the abrogated, what is replaced, and what is established. All of that is in a Book."

* *

Others said concerning this, what follows:

20512. al-Qasim told us: al-Husayn told us: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from his father, from Sayyar, from Ibn Abbas, that he asked Ka'b about "the Mother of the Book." He said: "Allah knows what He is going to create and what His creatures will do. Then He said to His knowledge: 'Be a Book,' and it became a Book."

[[Report 20512: "Sayyar" is the mawla of Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Mu'awiya. He related from Abu al-Darda', Ibn Abbas, and Abu Umama. Sulayman al-Taymi related from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-thiqat) as "Sayyar ibn Abd Allah." Ibn Hajar said: "We have not found anyone who named his father Abd Allah other than Ibn Hibban."
He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (2/2/161), and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/254), and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him.
In the printed edition alone it reads: "Shaybан."
The report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4: 68), attributing it additionally to Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (4: 538). In all of them it is "Sayyar," which is correct.]]

* *

Others said: it is the Reminder (al-dhikr).

Those who said this:

20513. al-Qasim told us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me. Abu Ja'far said: I do not know whether Ibn Jurayj is in the chain or not. He said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, he said: "The Reminder."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in terms of truth, is the saying of the one who said: "And with Him is the origin of the Book and its whole. That is because He, may He be remembered, informed that He effaces what He wills and establishes what He wills. Then He followed that with His saying: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, so it was clear that its meaning is: And with Him is the origin of what is established and what is effaced, and its whole is in a Book with Him."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿and establishes (wa-yuthbit)﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read: "wa-yuthabbit," with the doubling of the "ba'," meaning: he leaves it and confirms it in its state, so He does not efface it.

* *

Some of the Meccan reciters, some of the Basran reciters, and some of the Kufan reciters read: ﴿wa-yuthbit﴾ with the lightening, meaning: he writes.

* *

And we have already explained that its meaning, in our view, is the affirming of what is written and the leaving of it unerased, as we have explained. If that is so, then affirming it (al-tathbit) is the more fitting reading, and the emphatic form (al-tashdid) is more correct than the lightened form (al-takhfif). Yet the lightened form may also admit of being understood in the sense of the emphatic form, and the emphatic form in the sense of the lightened form, because their meanings are close.

* *

As for *al-mahw* (erasing), the Arabs have two dialects concerning it. The tribe of Mudar says: "*maḥawtu al-kitāba amḥūhu maḥwan*" ("I erased the writing, I erase it, erasing"), and the Revelation uses it: "*wa-maḥawtuhu amḥāhu maḥwan*" ("and I erased it, I erase it, erasing").

It is reported from some clans of Rabi'ah that they say: "*maḥaytu amḥā*" ("I erased, I erase"). [[This dialect is also attributed in *Lisan al-Arab* and elsewhere to Tayy. And "*amḥā*" has a fatha on the ḥā'. See *Majaz al-Qur'an* of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 334, and what preceded: 484, note: 2.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 40–41:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ (40)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Whether We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime, part of what We threaten these polytheists with, of punishment for their disbelief; or We take you before We show you that, your duty is only to submit to your Lord in what He has commanded you concerning conveying His message to them, not to seek their reform or their corruption. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 42:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those before them had already plotted, but to Allah belongs all plotting. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate abode﴾ (13:42).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Those before these polytheists of Quraysh, from the nations that passed before, had already plotted against the prophets and messengers of Allah. ﴿But to Allah belongs all plotting﴾ means: to Allah belong all the means of plotting, and it is in His hand and toward Him. The plotting of whoever plotted among them harms no one except the one whom He wills to harm by it. That is, the plotters did not harm anyone with their plotting except those whom Allah willed to be harmed by it. They harmed only themselves, because they incurred the anger of their Lord by it, until He destroyed them and saved His messengers. That is to say: likewise, these polytheists of Quraysh plot against you, O Muhammad, but Allah will save you from their plotting and will turn the harm of their plotting back upon them, not upon you. [[See the explanation of "al-makr" (plotting) above: 466, note 3, and the references there.]]

As for His saying: ﴿He knows what every soul earns﴾, it means: Your Lord, O Muhammad, knows what these polytheists of your people do, and what they strive at of plotting against you, and He knows all the deeds of all creation; nothing of them is hidden from Him [[See the explanation of "al-kasb" (earning) above in the language indexes.]] = ﴿and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate abode﴾, meaning: they will know, when they come before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, to whom the final outcome of the abode belongs, when they enter the Fire, and the believers in Allah and His Messenger will enter Paradise. [[See the explanation of "al-'uqba" (outcome) above: 472, note 5, and the references there.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the reading of this:

The reading of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra is: "wa-sa-ya'lamu al-kafiru" (in the singular), [[In the printed edition: "some people of Basra"; the wording is acceptable with or without this addition.]]

* *

As for the reading of the people of Kufa, they read it: ﴿wa-sa-ya'lamu al-kuffar﴾, in the plural.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter is the reading in the plural: ﴿wa-sa-ya'lamu al-kuffar﴾, because the report before it concerned their group, and the report after it about them continued, namely His saying: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you in death﴾, and after it His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: You are not a messenger﴾. It has been reported that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "wa-sa-ya'lamu al-kafirun" (plural with the masculine sound ending), and in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿wa-sa-ya'lamu alladhina kafaru﴾. All of this is evidence for the soundness of what we have chosen as the reading in this matter.

Interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and [sufficient is] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."﴾ [13:43]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty and Glorious is He says: And those who disbelieve in Allah from your people, O Muhammad, say, "You are not a messenger!" in denial of you and rejection of your prophethood [[See the explanation of "risalah" (message, mission) in the earlier word indices.]]. So say to them when they say that: ﴿Sufficient is Allah﴾, meaning: Say, "Allah is enough for me" [[See the explanation of "kafa" (suffices) earlier, 8:429.]] ﴿as a witness﴾, meaning: as a witness [[See the explanation of "shahid" (witness) in the earlier word indices.]] ﴿between me and you﴾, meaning: against me and against you, regarding my truthfulness and your lying ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾.

* *

As for "man" (whoever) when read in this way, it stands in the genitive position, coordinated with the name of Allah. This is how the readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) recite it, meaning: "and those who have knowledge of the Scripture," i.e., the books revealed before the Qur'an, such as the Torah and the Gospel. The exegetes also interpreted it according to this reading.

20540 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾: it is Abdullah ibn Salam.

20541 - ... He said: Yahya ibn Abbad narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾.

20542 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger"﴾, he said: It is the statement of the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture"﴾: [they are] people from among the People of the Book who used to bear witness to the truth and acknowledge it, and who knew that Muhammad was the Messenger of Allah, as it is related that among them was Abdullah ibn Salam.

20543 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾, he said: Among them were Abdullah ibn Salam, Salman al-Farisi, and Tamim al-Dari.

20544 - Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾, he said: It is Abdullah ibn Salam.

* *

It has been mentioned from a group of the earlier scholars that they used to read it: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitab" (and from Him was the Scripture made known), meaning: from Allah the Scripture was made known. [[In the manuscript, "'ulima" is vocalized as passive in both places; this first reading is attributed by Abu Hayyan in his tafsir (5:402) to Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn al-Sumayfa', and al-Hasan, as will come in reports 20547 and 20553. A second reading, also mentioned by Abu Hayyan, was recited by a large number of readers, including Ibn Abbas, with "min" likewise as a preposition: ﴿wa-min 'indihi 'ilmu al-kitab﴾. A third reading, unattributed: ﴿wa-min 'indihi 'ullima al-kitabu﴾ with a doubled lam and passive voice.

I have not found this first reading attributed to Ibn Abbas, but the following report, 20545, indicates that he recited it so, since the statement of Abu Ja'far is decisive that he intended this reading with "'ilm" in the passive, as is clear from report 20553 and his comment on it. See the following note.]]

Mention of those who related that from him:

20545 - Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata' narrated to us, from Harun, from Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyya, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah the Scripture was made known.

20546 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah.

20547 - ... He said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah the Scripture was made known. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated this hadith to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: It is Allah. Thus al-Hasan recited: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu".

20548 - ... He said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, similarly.

20549 - He said: Ali [ibn al-Ja'd] narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: It is Allah. Shu'ba said: I mentioned that to al-Hakam, and he said: Mujahid said the same.

20550 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: I heard Mansur ibn Zadhan relate from al-Hasan that he said regarding this verse: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah.

20551 - ... He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah the Scripture was made known.

20552 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah, the knowledge (ilm) of the Scripture. [[The word "'ilm" is vocalized with a kasra and sukun, since I suspect that al-Tabari therefore said: "Thus said Ibn Abd al-A'la." This matter rests in reality on transmission, and where is transmission today? Or on vocalization, and the manuscript is unvocalized, so I hope I have hit the meaning of the report. See the following report and its vocalization.]] Thus said Ibn Abd al-A'la.

20553 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to recite it: "Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has been made to know the Scripture from Allah'", meaning: the Scripture was made known from Allah, and its whole [meaning]. Abu Ja'far said: Bishr related this to us as "'ulima al-kitabu", and I think he erred in it, and that it is "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", [[ "'ilm" with kasra then sukun then damma.]] because his words "and its whole" is a noun, which cannot be coordinated with a past verb.

20554 - Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Harun: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", he said: from Allah the Scripture was made known.

20555 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", is it Abdullah ibn Salam? He said: This surah is Meccan, so how could it be Abdullah ibn Salam? He said: He used to recite it: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", meaning: from Allah. [[The word "'ilm" is vocalized in the passive in the manuscript.]]

20556 - Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the saying of Allah ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾: is it Abdullah ibn Salam? He said: How, when this surah is Meccan? Sa'id used to recite it: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu".

20557 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to me, from Awf, from al-Hasan; and Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, both said: "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", [[ "'ilm" vocalized in the passive in the manuscript.]] he said: from Allah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: A report has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) confirming this reading and this interpretation, though there is doubt regarding its chain, namely:

20558 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to me, from Harun al-A'war, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn Abdullah, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited "wa-min 'indihi 'ulima al-kitabu", meaning: with Allah the Scripture was made known. [[Abbad ibn al-Awwam al-Wasiti is reliable, one of Ahmad's teachers. Harun al-A'war is Harun ibn Musa al-Ataki, reliable, and the reciter with a known reading. This chain is interrupted (munqati'), because Harun al-A'war did not hear from al-Zuhri. Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7:155) and said: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in it is Sulayman ibn Arqam, who is abandoned (matruk)." Al-Suyuti also cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4:69), saying: Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Adi related it with a weak chain from Ibn Umar. Sulayman ibn Arqam, Abu Mu'adh al-Basri, narrates from al-Zuhri and is abandoned in hadith; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is worth nothing, not a fals," and Ibn Hibban said: "He was among those who reverse reports and narrate fabrications from reliable narrators." Harun al-A'war's narration was probably from Sulayman ibn Arqam, and he dropped him.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This report has no basis among the reliable transmitters from the students of al-Zuhri.

Given that this is so, and that the readers of the major cities, from the people of the Hijaz, Syria and Iraq, follow the other reading, namely: ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture﴾, the interpretation that accords with the meaning followed by the readers of the cities is more correct than what contradicts it [[In the printed edition: "mimman khalafahu" (from among those who opposed it), which differs from the manuscript without reflection.]], since a reading agreed upon by those people is more deserving of correctness.

"End of the tafsir of Surah al-Ra'd" [[After this in the manuscript:

"And praise be to Allah, abundant praise, as is befitting Him.

And may Allah bless Muhammad the Chosen, and his family, the people of truthfulness and fidelity, and greet abundantly.

To be followed, God willing, by: The tafsir of Surah Ibrahim."]]
